body:
Fixes #119. ## Summary The JS `--capture api` (export-html → markdown) path collapsed `
`-separated lines inside a list item into a single run, while the other three paths (Rust-API, JS-browser, Rust-browser) handled them correctly. This PR makes all four paths agree. ## Root cause Turndown's `replacementForNode` calls `content.trim()` on the inner markdown of any inline element whose `flankingWhitespace` is non-empty (`turndown.cjs.js:902`), which strips the trailing ` \n` hard break that the `
` rule emits. The Google Docs export-html commonly produces patterns like: ```html TAG1 – Definition one.
TAG2 ``` The `` has leading whitespace, so its inner content is trimmed — and the `
`'s hard break disappears with it. Result: `**TAG1** – Definition one.**TAG2**` on a single line. A second, smaller bug compounded it: `js/src/postprocess.js` collapsed `text \n` → `text \n`, eating the two trailing spaces that mark a CommonMark hard break. ## Fix 1. **`js/src/lib.js`** — new helper `liftBrFromInlineEdges($)` that hoists any `
` sitting at the leading or trailing edge of an inline parent (`span`, `a`, `strong`, `em`, …) out of that parent before Turndown runs. The break then attaches at the parent (block) level, which Turndown handles correctly. Wired into both `convertHtmlToMarkdown` (used by `--capture api`) and `convertHtmlToMarkdownEnhanced`. 2. **`js/src/postprocess.js`** — added negative lookahead `(?!\n)` to the double-space collapse regex so the two trailing spaces of a CommonMark hard break survive postprocessing. ## Tests New regression tests with a shared fixture (`list-item-with-br.html`) that mirrors the realistic Google Docs export-html structure that triggered the bug: - `js/tests/unit/html2md-br-in-list-item.test.js` — fails before fix, passes after. - `rust/tests/integration/html2md_br_in_list_item.rs` — passes (Rust converter never had the bug; this guards parity). ## Test plan - [x] `cd js && npm test -- tests/unit` — 254/258 pass; the 4 failures are pre-existing `browser.test.js` failures from a missing Playwright Chromium binary in the sandbox, unrelated to this change. - [x] `cd js && npm test -- tests/unit/html2md-br-in-list-item.test.js tests/unit/html2md.test.js tests/unit/postprocess.test.js tests/unit/gdocs.test.js tests/unit/gdocs-preprocess.test.js tests/unit/html2md-ol-numbering.test.js` — 104/104 pass. - [x] `cd rust && cargo test` — 92 unit + integration tests pass, 0 failed. - [x] `cd js && npm run lint` — 0 errors (warnings are all pre-existing). - [x] `cd js && npx prettier --check` on changed files — all formatted. ## Files changed - `js/src/lib.js` — `liftBrFromInlineEdges` helper + two call sites. - `js/src/postprocess.js` — `(?!\n)` lookahead to preserve hard breaks. - `js/.changeset/issue-119-br-in-list-item.md` — patch changeset. - `js/tests/fixtures/list-item-with-br.html`, `js/tests/unit/html2md-br-in-list-item.test.js` — JS regression test. - `rust/tests/fixtures/list-item-with-br.html`, `rust/tests/integration/html2md_br_in_list_item.rs`, `rust/tests/integration/mod.rs` — Rust parity test. - `experiments/repro-br-*.mjs` — reproduction scripts that pinpointed the bug.

title: Number consecutive top-level <ol>s continuously across JS and Rust (fixes #118)
body:
Fixes #118. ## Problem JS and Rust HTML→Markdown converters emitted different ordered-list numbering for the same input: - **JS (Turndown)**: restarted counter per `
    ` but honoured `
      `. - **Rust (html2md)**: restarted counter per `
        ` and ignored `
          `. Same HTML → different `.md`, breaking parity for documents with multiple top-level `
            `s or explicit `start=`. ## Fix Aligned both implementations on **continuous numbering across consecutive top-level `
              `s in document order, with `
                ` honoured** (resets the running counter to N for that list, subsequent lists continue from there). - **Top-level** = not nested inside another `
                  ` or `
                    `. Nested lists keep their own per-list `1.` numbering, matching the prior behaviour. - Setext heading underlines (`---`/`===`) are detected so a `1. Headings` line followed by a setext underline isn't misidentified as a list item. ### JS (`js/src/lib.js`) New `applyContinuousOrderedListNumbering($)` runs as a cheerio pre-pass in both `convertHtmlToMarkdown` and `convertHtmlToMarkdownEnhanced`. Walks each top-level `
                      ` and writes a `start` attribute so Turndown emits the correct numbers. Honours an existing `start="N"` (resets the counter and preserves the attribute). ### Rust (`rust/src/markdown.rs`) `html2md` ignores `start=`, so we go DOM → numbers → markdown post-pass: 1. `compute_top_level_ordered_list_item_numbers` walks the parsed DOM and produces a `Vec` with one number per direct `
                    1. ` of every top-level `
                        `, in document order, honouring `start="N"`. 2. `renumber_top_level_ordered_list_lines` iterates `html2md` output line by line and replaces unindented `^\d+\.\s` line prefixes with sequential numbers from the precomputed `Vec`. Indented (nested-list) lines are left alone. Setext heading underlines are detected via next-line lookahead. ## Tests Shared fixture `tests/fixtures/ol-continuous-numbering.html` (identical content in both `js/` and `rust/`) covers two consecutive top-level `
                          `s plus an `
                            `: ```html
                            1. First
                            2. Second

                            Some prose between lists.

                            1. Third
                            2. Fourth
                            1. Top-level numbered heading.
                            ``` - `js/tests/unit/html2md-ol-numbering.test.js` — passes ✓ - `rust/tests/integration/html2md_ol_numbering.rs` — passes ✓ Both assert `1. **First** ... 2. **Second** ... 3. **Third** ... 4. **Fourth** ... 13. **Top-level**`. ## Test plan - [x] `cargo test` — 93 integration + 92 unit + 2 doctests all pass - [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean - [x] `node --experimental-vm-modules ./node_modules/.bin/jest tests/unit` — only failures are the pre-existing browser tests blocked by missing Chrome in this env; new test passes - [x] `npx prettier --check` — clean on changed files - [x] No regression in existing gdocs / heading-numbering tests

title: Preserve hierarchical heading numbering (13, 13.1) in API path
body:

## Summary Fixes #110. JS API-mode/public-export Google Docs capture now keeps multi-paragraph table cells as valid GFM table rows: - Google Docs export table-cell paragraphs are flattened with `

` separators. - Turndown preserves `
` as literal inline HTML when the break is inside a `` or ``, instead of turning it into physical Markdown newlines. - A focused regression test covers the preprocessed HTML and final Markdown row. - Added a patch changeset for `@link-assistant/web-capture`. - Archived issue/PR/research data and analysis in the issue case study: https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/issue-110-9712e1c70a94/docs/case-studies/issue-110/README.md ## Reproduction Before the fix, this Google Docs export shape: ```html

First paragraph.

Second paragraph.

Third paragraph.

``` became Markdown with hard-break newlines inside a pipe table cell, which terminates or corrupts the GFM table. After the fix, the row contains inline breaks and stays on one physical Markdown line: ```md | First paragraph.

Second paragraph.

title: --capture browser: numbered lists rendered as <ul> + non-list paragraphs misclassified as <blockquote>
body:
**TL;DR:** Browser-mode (`--capture browser`) Google Docs extraction has two bugs that affect both the Rust and JS CLIs identically. Both stem from heuristics in the `DOCS_modelChunk` parser that were over-fitted to the project's existing public test fixture and fail on real documents.

## Versions affected

- `web-capture` (Rust crate): **0.3.9** (latest published)
- `@link-assistant/web-capture` (npm): **1.7.17** (latest published)

Both fully reproduce the bugs below.

## Public reproducer doc

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Rvaod_u2wgkAUNdXG-e29yQem-P36KAQ/edit (Anyone with the link, viewer)

This is a copy of the existing markdown-feature test fixture with a new **Section 15** added that contains three small structures designed to trigger the bugs. The original sections (1–14) still pass — the regressions only show in the new Section 15.

## Bug 1 — Numbered list rendered as `<ul>` (markdown `- `)

### Reproduction

In Section 15, subsection A of the public reproducer:

```
1. Apple
2. Banana
3. Cherry
```

This is an ordered list (decimal markers) in the source. Confirm via `--capture api`, which preserves it correctly:

`--capture api` markdown:
```
1. Apple
2. Banana
3. Cherry
```

`--capture browser` markdown (BUG):
```
- Apple
- Banana
- Cherry
```

### Root cause (Rust)

`rust/src/gdocs.rs:2473`:

```rust
fn infer_ordered_list(list: &ListMeta, text: &str) -> bool {
    let ordered_id = matches!(
        list.id.as_str(),
        "kix.list.7" | "kix.list.8" | "kix.list.9" | "kix.list.10" | "kix.list.11" | "kix.list.13"
    );
    ordered_id
        && (text.contains("ordered")
            || text.contains("Parent item")
            || text.contains("Child item")
            || text.contains("Grandchild item")
            || text.contains("First item")
            || text.contains("Second item")
            || text.contains("Third item")
            || text.contains("Ordered child"))
}
```

This is a hardcoded list-ID allowlist combined with a content-substring check. It returns `false` for any document whose lists don't have one of those specific IDs and whose items don't contain those specific substrings — i.e. for essentially every real document. The only doc it works on is the existing public test fixture, because the heuristic was fitted to that fixture's content.

### Root cause (JS)

`js/src/gdocs.js` ~L946:

```js
function inferOrderedList(list, text) {
  if (
    /ordered|^\d+(?:\.|\))|child \d|parent item|child item|grandchild item|first item|second item|third item/i.test(text)
  ) {
    return /^kix\.list\.(7|8|9|10|11|13)$/u.test(list.id);
  }
  return false;
}
```

Identical defective approach.

### Why a heuristic at all?

I confirmed by capturing live `DOCS_modelChunk` data (using a `Object.defineProperty` hook installed via `addInitScript` before page load) that the chunk does NOT carry glyph-type / ordered-vs-unordered information for the list. The schema has:

- `ty="as"` mutations with `st="list"` carry only `ls_id` (list ID), `ls_ts` (text-styling for the marker), and `ls_c` (with sub-fields `c_cs`/`c_tdai` — neither encodes glyph type).
- A full keyword search across the chunk for `ordered|decimal|numbered|bullet|disc|circle|square|lower-latin|lower-roman` returns zero matches.

So the parser cannot answer "is this list ordered?" from `DOCS_modelChunk` alone.

The api-mode HTML export DOES have this information — Google embeds it in the `<style>` block as CSS counter rules:

```css
.lst-kix_8pt4o74780u8-0>li:before{content:"" counter(lst-ctn-kix_8pt4o74780u8-0,decimal) ". "}
```

The `decimal` argument (vs absent / `disc` / `none`) tells you the glyph is numeric.

### Suggested fix

Two reasonable paths:

1. **Always fetch api-mode HTML alongside browser-mode** (a tiny, fast public export request) and merge: walk the api-mode CSS to build `Map<list_id, glyph_type>`, then use that to decide `ordered` for each list seen in the chunk. This requires the doc to be public-export-capable; for private docs the user is already authenticated to do `--capture browser`, so an `/export?format=html` request with the same cookies should also succeed.

2. **Default to `<ol>` when `ps_il > 0` AND `ps_ifl < ps_il` AND the marker text from `ls_ts` is a digit/letter sequence**. This is also a heuristic but a much more principled one (the per-paragraph `ps_il`/`ps_ifl` fields are stable and the `ls_ts` text-styling is per-list).

Either way, drop the hardcoded list-ID allowlist and content-substring regex.

## Bug 2 — Continuation paragraphs misclassified as `<blockquote>`

### Reproduction

In Section 15, subsection B of the public reproducer:

> 1. Step one
>
>    Continuation paragraph that is not a list item. Same indent as Step one.
>
> 1. Step two

(Created in the editor by: type "1. Step one", Enter, Backspace to drop the marker but keep the indent, type the continuation paragraph, Enter, re-apply numbered list, "Step two".)

`--capture api` markdown: keeps the continuation as a regular paragraph (no blockquote prefix).

`--capture browser` markdown (BUG):
```
- Step one

> Continuation paragraph that is not a list item. Same indent as Step one.

- Step two
```

The non-list paragraph between Step one and Step two is emitted as a blockquote.

### Root cause (Rust)

`rust/src/gdocs.rs:2458`:

```rust
} else if paragraph_style.is_some_and(|style| {
    style.indent_start > 0.0
        && (style.indent_start - style.indent_first_line).abs() < f64::EPSILON
}) {
    meta.quote = true;
}
```

The heuristic is "any non-list paragraph with `indent_start > 0` and `indent_start == indent_first_line`" → blockquote. But that's exactly the shape of a Google Docs list-continuation paragraph (when you Backspace out the marker, the indent is preserved equally on first-line and subsequent lines).

### Suggested fix

Either:
1. Cross-check with api-mode HTML: api correctly emits `<blockquote>` only when the source has one. Use it as the source of truth for which indented paragraphs are quotes.
2. Tighten the heuristic: require either (a) a known blockquote paragraph style (`HEADING_*`-equivalent style id for blockquote), or (b) the indent to be substantially larger than typical list-item indent (e.g. `> 36pt`, the typical level-0 list indent), or (c) the paragraph not to be sandwiched between list items.

## Why both bugs were missed by CI

`gdocs-public-doc.test.js` and `gdocs_public_doc.rs` test against the existing public fixture (`1f5zI2xOFpKa90v0GjamO_t7lqSdzMlaM`). That fixture's content matches the heuristic regexes ("First item", "Second item", "Parent item", etc.) and its list IDs are within the hardcoded allowlist. So the tests pass for reasons that don't generalize.

Suggested test additions: capture the public reproducer doc above (or a similar synthetic one) and assert both:
- numbered lists with content like "Apple", "Banana" produce `1. … 2. …` markdown, not `- … - …`
- list-item continuation paragraphs do NOT become blockquotes

## Side note (not blocking)

In the same Section 15 of the reproducer, browser-mode also wraps the entire section's text in italics (`*Apple*`, `*Banana*`, `*Step one*`, etc.) — likely italic-style leakage from the preceding italic "End of Markdown Feature Test Document" line. API-mode renders the same text upright. This may be a separate text-style range tracking bug; mentioning here for visibility but happy to file separately if preferred.

## Tested with

- macOS 14 (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Chromium fetched by `chromiumoxide` (Rust) / Playwright (JS)
- Both CLIs installed via their published distributions (`npm i -g`, `cargo install`)

title: --capture browser: flaky / potentially incomplete captures — neither CLI waits for DOCS_modelChunk stream to quiesce
body:
## Summary

Both CLIs' `--capture browser` path uses a **time-based** wait to decide when `DOCS_modelChunk` data is \"ready\" for extraction. This is a heuristic, not correctness:

- **Rust** returns on the **first non-empty poll** → observable flake: large docs with >1 model chunk sometimes return a truncated capture (only the first chunk).
- **JS** waits a **flat 8000 ms** after `domcontentloaded` → works for docs that finish streaming within 8 s but has no guarantee for larger docs.

The right design is \"**poll until chunks stop changing**\" — i.e. quiescence detection with a configurable stability window and a hard timeout. Both CLIs should converge on that design.

## Observed flake (Rust)

Reinstalled Rust `0.3.8` in isolation, ran `--capture browser` against the same Google Doc 5 times back-to-back. The doc has enough content to be streamed across multiple `DOCS_modelChunk` assignments (the editor emits chunks progressively for bigger documents — size matters here, not content).

```
run 1: chunks=1 cid_urls=39 blocks=26 images=15 text_bytes=6489   # TRUNCATED
run 2: chunks=2 cid_urls=39 blocks=66 images=39 text_bytes=11553  # complete
run 3: chunks=1 cid_urls=39 blocks=26 images=15 text_bytes=6489   # TRUNCATED
run 4: chunks=1 cid_urls=39 blocks=26 images=15 text_bytes=6489   # TRUNCATED
run 5: chunks=2 cid_urls=39 blocks=66 images=39 text_bytes=11553  # complete
```

The image map (`cid_urls=39`) loads fully in both variants — only the `DOCS_modelChunk` stream is affected. When the capture is truncated, **more than half the document content is silently missing** from the archive (`document.md`, `document.html`, and `images/`).

JS `1.7.16` in isolation on the same doc returned 39 images / 280 markdown lines **5 times out of 5** — so on documents that finish streaming well under 8 s, JS's fixed wait happens to cover the race. On a doc that takes >8 s it would fail the same way.

## Root-cause pointers

**Rust — `rust/src/gdocs.rs`, `wait_for_google_docs_model_chunks` (~L1035)**:

```rust
while started.elapsed() < GDOCS_EDITOR_MODEL_WAIT {  // 30 s cap
    let model_data = ...;  // Runtime.evaluate → read window.__captured_chunks
    if !model_data.chunks.is_empty() {
        return Ok(model_data);  // <-- returns on FIRST non-empty, not on quiescence
    }
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
}
```

Every 250 ms the loop asks the page \"how many chunks do you have?\" and returns the moment the answer is ≥1. If Google Docs emits chunk 1 at t≈1.2 s and chunk 2 at t≈1.8 s, the 1.25 s poll will happily return with just chunk 1.

**JS — `js/src/gdocs.js`, `captureGoogleDocWithBrowser` (~L413)**:

```js
await page.goto(editUrl, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded', timeout: 60000 });
await waitForPage(page, waitMs);   // waitMs defaults to 8000 ms — FLAT SLEEP
const modelData = await evaluateOnPage(page, () => {
  const chunks = [...(window.__captured_chunks || [])];
  ...
});
```

The `Object.defineProperty(window, 'DOCS_modelChunk', { set })` hook installed at L523 keeps recording chunks throughout the 8 s sleep, so late chunks *are* captured — but only if they arrive within 8 s. There is no verification that the stream has settled; a slow network or a big doc will silently lose tail chunks.

## Proposed fix (both CLIs — same algorithm)

Replace the time-based wait with a quiescence loop, parameterized by a **stability window** and a **hard timeout**:

```
stability_window = 1500 ms   (chunks must stop changing for this long)
hard_timeout     = 30000 ms  (give up if still churning)
poll_interval    = 250 ms    (how often to snapshot)
```

Algorithm (pseudocode, applies to both JS and Rust):

```
last_fingerprint = None
stable_since     = None
deadline         = now + hard_timeout
while now < deadline:
    fingerprint = (chunks.length, total_chunk_payload_size)
    if fingerprint == last_fingerprint and fingerprint.0 > 0:
        if stable_since is None: stable_since = now
        if now - stable_since >= stability_window: return chunks   # quiesced
    else:
        stable_since     = None
        last_fingerprint = fingerprint
    sleep(poll_interval)
raise TimeoutError(\"DOCS_modelChunk stream did not quiesce within hard_timeout\")
```

Notes:

- `total_chunk_payload_size` in the fingerprint catches the edge case where chunk count stays the same but an existing chunk's contents grow (observed occasionally — Docs appends to the same array). Just counting chunks isn't sufficient.
- The `fingerprint.0 > 0` guard prevents declaring quiescence before the first chunk arrives.
- `stability_window` of 1.5 s is a starting point — inspired by what a human \"looks idle\" threshold would be. Make it env-configurable (`WEB_CAPTURE_GDOCS_STABILITY_MS`) so large/slow docs can bump it.
- `hard_timeout` of 30 s matches Rust's current `GDOCS_EDITOR_MODEL_WAIT`. Keep it env-configurable too (`WEB_CAPTURE_GDOCS_MAX_WAIT_MS`).
- The return must never happen purely from elapsed time; the only success path is \"no changes for `stability_window`\". A timeout return should either error (strict mode) or return with a warning log (\"returned possibly-incomplete capture; set WEB_CAPTURE_GDOCS_MAX_WAIT_MS higher\").

## Why this also removes JS's hidden flake

JS's current 8000 ms wait works for the docs in existing test fixtures, but that's coincidence. On a slow network, an 8 s wait after `domcontentloaded` may also return before chunk streaming finishes. Once both CLIs adopt quiescence-based waiting, behavior becomes deterministic across network speed, doc size, and machine load — small docs return in ~1.5 s, large ones take as long as they take, nothing is silently truncated.

## Testing

Add a deterministic regression test that **forces non-trivial chunking** without depending on a specific private document:

1. **Synthetic public fixture.** Create a public Google Doc in CI's fixture set where the body is large enough to reliably emit >1 `DOCS_modelChunk`. A practical threshold is ~8-12 KB of document text: enough paragraphs of Lorem ipsum, a handful of inline images (use `docs.google.com/`-hosted test pngs), no unusual formatting required. The exact cutoff Google uses for chunking is implementation-defined, but in our testing docs with `text_bytes >= 10000` reliably emit ≥2 chunks.

2. **Two assertions in `gdocs_public_doc` live tests** (both languages):
   - `chunks >= 2` (or `text_bytes >= 10000`) — forces us to actually exercise the multi-chunk path.
   - **Stability check**: run capture N times (N=5 is enough); **image count and `text_bytes` must be identical across all runs**. This is the regression guard — if a run truncates, it'll stand out in the N-sample comparison.

3. **Log the stability diagnostic.** The `parsed Google Docs editor model` info line already prints `chunks`, `cid_urls`, `blocks`, `images`, `text_bytes`. Add `poll_count` and `stable_for_ms` to it so that operational issues (\"this doc took 14 s to quiesce\") are visible in production logs.

4. **No changes needed to existing test fixtures** — the issue-90 reference doc (`1f5zI2xOFpKa90v0GjamO_t7lqSdzMlaM`) is small and emits `chunks=1`, which is why it didn't surface this bug. Keep it; add the new multi-chunk fixture alongside.

## Repro recipe (without private docs)

1. Go to docs.google.com and create a new document.
2. Paste Lorem ipsum until `Tools → Word count → Characters` shows ≥ 10000.
3. Insert 4-6 `Insert → Image → Upload` blocks scattered through the doc.
4. `Share → Anyone with the link → Viewer`. Copy the link.
5. Put that URL in `$URL`, then:

```bash
# Rust
cargo install web-capture
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  rm -rf run$i && mkdir run$i && cd run$i
  web-capture \"$URL\" --archive zip --capture browser 2>&1 \\
    | grep \"parsed Google Docs editor model\"
  cd ..
done
cargo uninstall web-capture
```

Expect: most runs show `chunks=2, images=<N>, text_bytes=<big>`, but a fraction show `chunks=1, images=<~half>, text_bytes=<~half>`. The fraction depends on machine speed and network — on a fast Mac (M-series, good connection) we saw 3/5 truncated runs.

```bash
# JS (for contrast — no flake on sub-8-s docs, but same design flaw)
npm i -g @link-assistant/web-capture
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  rm -rf run$i && mkdir run$i && cd run$i
  web-capture \"$URL\" --archive zip --capture browser > /dev/null 2>&1
  unzip -p \"$(find . -name document.zip)\" document.md | wc -l
  cd ..
done
npm uninstall -g @link-assistant/web-capture
```

JS is likely to come out stable at 8 s, but increase doc size to ≥ 30-40 KB text to push past the 8 s window and you'll see it truncate too.

## Environment

- JS: `@link-assistant/web-capture@1.7.16` on Node 20.19.4 (package declares `node >=22 <23`).
- Rust: `web-capture 0.3.8` (crates.io), stable toolchain.
- Each CLI installed in full isolation (other uninstalled first) to rule out PATH shadowing.
- macOS 24.6.0.

## Related

- #104 (merged) — fixed HTML rendering parity; exposed this underlying capture-completeness bug, because divergence caused by this flake was previously attributed to the rendering difference.
- #102 — `--capture api` fidelity defects (separate issue).

title: Fix Google Docs browser-model HTML parity
body:
Fixes #104 ## Summary - Keep Google Docs soft line breaks outside inline bold/italic/strike/link markup in both JS and Rust HTML renderers, so marked multi-line runs serialize as per-line marked segments around `
`. - Keep Markdown markers balanced across embedded newlines in both renderers. - Align Rust browser-model parsing with JS by treating Google Docs soft breaks as unstyled separator nodes, preventing styled runs from spanning the break in the parsed block model. - Preserve Rust browser-model image `width` and `height` metadata and emit matching `` attributes in rendered HTML. - Add the issue 104 fixture, expected HTML/Markdown outputs, before/after logs, and case-study notes under `docs/case-studies/issue-104/`. ## Reproduction The shared fixture `docs/case-studies/issue-104/fixtures/multiline-marked-inline-image-model.json` reproduces the failing editor-model shape: a bold multi-line paragraph with soft breaks and an inline image between marked lines. Before the fix: - JS direct rendering emitted `Alpha
Beta` for a styled text node with an embedded newline. - Rust parsed the first two bold soft-broken lines into one styled text node and emitted `Line one
Line two`. - Rust omitted browser-model image dimensions from ``. After the fix, both CLIs match `multiline-marked-inline-image.expected.html` and keep markdown markers per line. ## Verification - `cd js && npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/unit/gdocs.test.js --runInBand` - `cd js && npm run check` - `cd js && npm run format:check` - `cd js && npm test -- --runInBand --testPathIgnorePatterns=tests/unit/browser.test.js --testPathIgnorePatterns=tests/integration/browser-engines.test.js --testPathIgnorePatterns=tests/integration/habr-article.test.js --testPathIgnorePatterns=tests/e2e/docker.test.js` - `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` - `cd rust && cargo test --test integration gdocs:: -- --nocapture` - `cd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cd rust && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` - `cd rust && cargo test` - `git diff --check` A broader JS Jest run excluding only Docker was also attempted and is preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-104/js-test-non-docker.log`; it reached browser integration suites and failed because the local Playwright Chromium binary is not installed. The hermetic non-browser/non-Docker suite passed separately.

title: --capture browser: JS and Rust emit different HTML from the same editor model (strong/br grouping), cascading into different markdown
body:
## Summary `--capture browser` in the two CLIs parses the Google Docs editor model into the **same abstract block structure** (paragraphs with `content[]` of text runs + image nodes, plus `list` / `quote` / `style` / `horizontalRule` flags), but the **HTML serializer diverges** — so `document.html` in the archive already differs before html→markdown runs. The markdown defects cascade from that. On simple documents the difference is invisible; on documents where a single bold/italic span wraps multiple lines (soft line breaks, `Shift+Enter`) and contains an inline image, the two outputs diverge significantly. ## Repro (public, synthetic — no private data) Create a brand-new public Google Doc with this exact structure (copy into the editor as-is): > **Bulleted list item (click "Bulleted list" in the toolbar, then type):** > > Line one of bold text. \[Shift+Enter\] > Line two of bold text. \[Shift+Enter\] > \[Enter to start a new line, Shift+Enter again\] > Line three of bold text. > > Now place the cursor between line two and line three, and **insert an image** via Insert → Image → Upload. Select the entire list item (all three lines + image) and apply **Bold** (`Ctrl/⌘+B`). Make the document public (\"Anyone with the link\"). Then, in an empty directory: ```bash # isolated JS npm install -g @link-assistant/web-capture web-capture \"$DOC_URL\" --archive zip --capture browser unzip -p data/web-capture/**/document.zip document.html > js.html npm uninstall -g @link-assistant/web-capture # isolated Rust cargo install web-capture web-capture \"$DOC_URL\" --archive zip --capture browser unzip -p data/web-capture/**/document.zip document.html > rust.html cargo uninstall web-capture diff js.html rust.html ``` ## Observed The two `document.html` files differ structurally around the bold multi-line run with inline image: **JS emits per-run `` elements, closed across `
`:** ```html
  • Line one of bold text.
    Line two of bold text.

    Line three of bold text.
``` **Rust emits a single `` wrapping the whole multi-line run, broken by `
` inside it:** ```html
  • Line one of bold text.
    Line two of bold text.

    Line three of bold text.
``` Two other consistent deltas visible in the HTML output: - **JS** emits `` with `width=\"…\" height=\"…\"` attributes taken from the editor model; **Rust** emits `` with no dimensions. - The two HTML files use **different pretty-printing**: JS uses 2-space indentation with inner content indented; Rust uses 4-space-ish indentation with `
` lines inside ``. That is purely whitespace, not structure, but it does make the files non-byte-identical even when the tag tree matches. ## Markdown cascade When the two HTMLs are converted to markdown (JS: turndown, Rust: html2md), the `` grouping difference produces the observable markdown defects: - **JS** output: `**Line one**\n**Line two**\n**Line three**` — every line ends with a clean bold pair. - **Rust** output: `**Line one\nLine two` … image … `Line three**` — bold markers open and close only at the boundaries of the outer ``, leaving middle lines unbolded in rendered markdown. On pages with many such runs, stray `**` lines appear where html2md lifted the closing `` to its own line. This matches what we see on internal test corpora where multi-line bold runs with inline images are common — the two CLIs diverge on those runs while agreeing perfectly on well-formed single-line bold spans (see issue #102 observations, where `--capture browser` outputs on the issue-90 reference doc were byte-identical — that doc has no multi-line bold runs). ## Root cause pointer Both CLIs share the algorithm; they disagree on **serialization of consecutive text runs with the same active marks across soft line breaks** inside a paragraph/list/blockquote. - JS: `js/src/gdocs.js` → `renderContentHtml` (around L1197) calls `renderMarkedHtml` (L1215) per `ContentNode`, which re-opens/closes `` for every run. A paragraph with three bold runs around an image produces three `` elements. - Rust: `rust/src/gdocs.rs` → `render_content_html` (L2292) also calls `render_marked_html` per node, but the upstream parser appears to combine consecutive bold runs (including those containing `\n`) into a single `ContentNode` with embedded newlines. `render_marked_html` at L2326 then emits one `A
B`. When such a combined run is split by an image, the parser emits two combined runs — hence the \"bold – image – bold\" pattern visible in Rust's HTML but \"bold – /bold – image – bold – /bold – image – bold\" in JS. So the fix is either: 1. **Converge on JS's convention**: the Rust parser should keep consecutive runs with a newline between them as separate `ContentNode`s (or the HTML renderer should split on `\n` and re-wrap each segment). This would make Rust's output look like JS's (per-line ``), and markdown would come out with clean per-line `**...**`. 2. **Converge on Rust's convention**: the JS parser should merge adjacent runs with matching marks into a single node with embedded `\n`, and both HTML renderers should emit one `` per merged run. Markdown converters would need to be taught to re-wrap `…
…` as `**line1**\n**line2**` rather than treating it as one long bold span across newlines (otherwise Rust's current markdown defect stays). Convention (1) is cleaner because it produces markdown that survives round-tripping in every renderer we tested. Convention (2) requires downstream fixes in both html→markdown libraries. ## Ask 1. **Pick a single serialization convention** for multi-line bold/italic/strike runs and the `` attribute set, and implement it identically in both `js/src/gdocs.js` and `rust/src/gdocs.rs`. The `document.html` inside the archive should be byte-identical (modulo whitespace) between the two CLIs for any given input document. 2. **Bring `` attributes in sync**: either both emit `width`/`height` (JS today) or neither does (Rust today). Downstream markdown and reader-mode viewers behave better with the dimensions preserved, so option A is preferable. 3. **Cross-CLI HTML parity test**: extend `gdocs_public_doc` tests (both JS and Rust) with an assertion that normalized `document.html` is identical across the two CLIs for the #90 reference document *plus* a new public fixture that exercises multi-line marked runs with inline images. The fixture should live in `docs/case-studies/` so it's version-controlled. 4. **If multiple editor-model extraction paths exist** (e.g. DOCS_modelChunk vs. rendered DOM fallback), keep both mechanisms available and make them selectable via a flag (`--gdocs-source model|dom|auto`, default `auto`). But sync the *rendering* from the parsed model across languages regardless of which extraction path was used. Based on reading the two `gdocs` modules, both CLIs currently use the DOCS_modelChunk path exclusively; this is a \"keep it that way, add fallbacks behind a flag if you need them\" recommendation, not a \"multiple paths exist today\" claim. 5. **Reference target**: the archived `document.html` should be as close as possible to what the Google Docs editor would itself output for a file → download → HTML of the same doc. That gives a stable, external ground truth both CLIs can be measured against. ## Environment - **JS:** `@link-assistant/web-capture@1.7.14` (npm, installed in isolation) - **Rust:** `web-capture 0.3.6` (crates.io, installed in isolation) - Reproduced with each CLI installed alone (other uninstalled first) to rule out PATH shadowing. - macOS 24.6.0. ## Related - #90 — reference markdown round-trip document (closed; this is a follow-up exposing a class of bugs the reference doc doesn't cover). - #102 — `--capture api` fidelity defects (separate issue; `--capture browser` is significantly better but still diverges as shown above).

title: --capture api (public-export) produces degraded markdown vs --capture browser in both CLIs (v1.7.14 / v0.3.6)
body:
Follow-up to #90 (closed). Installed the published CLIs and re-ran the reference test document from that issue:

- `npm install -g @link-assistant/web-capture` → `1.7.14`
- `cargo install web-capture --force` → `0.3.6`

## TL;DR

- `--capture browser` in both CLIs produces **byte-identical** markdown that matches the reference almost perfectly — this path is in great shape.
- `--capture api` (public-export) in both CLIs produces **visibly degraded** markdown vs the reference, in different ways per language.
- Image extraction is correct in all four runs.

We'd like `--capture api` brought as close to `--capture browser` fidelity as the public-export HTML pipeline allows. See "Ask" at the bottom.

## Repro

```
URL="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1f5zI2xOFpKa90v0GjamO_t7lqSdzMlaM/edit"
web-capture "$URL" --archive zip --capture api     -o api.zip
web-capture "$URL" --archive zip --capture browser -o browser.zip
```

Reference: `docs/case-studies/issue-90/reference/markdown-test-document.md`.

## `--capture browser` — reference fidelity ✅

Rust and JS browser outputs are `diff`-identical. Every section, list, table, nested formatting, strikethrough, blockquote, and image in the reference is preserved. Only cosmetic deltas vs the reference (hr rendered as `---` not 72 dashes, nested-list indent 4 spaces vs 2, unpadded table cells) — all semantically equivalent.

## JS `--capture api` defects

- Escaped dots in headings: `## 1\. Headings` (also `2\.`, `3\.` …)
- Single-tilde strikethrough: `~Strikethrough~` instead of `~~Strikethrough~~`
- Tables mangled — each cell on its own line with blank paragraphs:
  ```
  | 
  Feature

   | 

  Supported
  …
  ```
- Blockquote paragraphs split into separate blockquotes instead of one multi-paragraph quote:
  ```
  > This is a single-level blockquote…

  > This is a multi-paragraph blockquote.

  > This is the second paragraph inside the same blockquote.
  ```
- Nested list indentation flattened — children dedent to top level.

## Rust `--capture api` defects (different set)

- Setext-style headings (`==========`, `----------`) instead of ATX.
- `*` bullets instead of `-`.
- Nested list indentation flattened.
- Blockquote paragraphs wrapped with extra blank `>` lines:
  ```
  >
  >
  > This is a single-level blockquote…
  >
  >
  ```
- Italic markers leak into heading text: `#### *Heading level 4* ####`.
- Tables use padded columns but with italic leakage in some cells.

## Images ✅ (all four runs)

Four PNGs extracted with correct dimensions (200×100, 300×150, 150×150, 150×150). 1-byte differences vs local reference are expected — Google Docs re-encodes on export.

## Ask

1. **Bring `--capture api` as close to `--capture browser` fidelity as possible.** Route the public-export HTML through the same block / list / table / blockquote / inline renderer used by the editor-model path, or add a normalization pass that fixes the defects above (`\.`/`\!`/`\(` escapes, single vs double tildes, merged blockquote paragraphs, nested-list indent preservation, ATX headings, `-` bullets, italic marker leakage in headings). The existing `gdocs_public_doc::live` tests in both CLIs already normalize these escapes before asserting — the normalizer could move into the capture pipeline itself.

2. **Keep the CI coverage and tighten it as fidelity improves.** Live tests already run in CI (`GDOCS_INTEGRATION=true`) — see [`.github/workflows/js.yml` L201-205](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/main/.github/workflows/js.yml#L201-L205) and [`.github/workflows/rust.yml` L172-177](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/main/.github/workflows/rust.yml#L172-L177). As defects are fixed, please remove the matching `normalizeEscapes` / `replace("\\.", ".")` calls in `js/tests/integration/gdocs-public-doc.test.js` and `rust/tests/integration/gdocs_public_doc.rs` so the assertions lock in the improvements and prevent regressions. Ideally add explicit `--capture api` parity asserts alongside the existing `--capture browser` ones (same feature checklist, same doc, both capture modes).

## Environment

- **JS:** `@link-assistant/web-capture@1.7.14` on Node 20.19.4 (note: package declares `node >=22 <23` — but the CLI ran and the issue reproduces on supported Node as well per the case-study).
- **Rust:** `web-capture 0.3.6`, stable toolchain, macOS 24.6.0.

title: v0.3.4 / v1.7.12: Rust browser capture always times out on Google Docs, tables have ghost columns, images not downloaded
body:
## Critical: Rust `--capture browser` always times out on Google Docs

It is unacceptable that `--capture browser` does not work in the Rust CLI. This is the primary feature differentiator from `--capture api`, and when a user explicitly requests browser capture, it must work — not silently fall back to a degraded path.

### Root cause

The Rust browser capture uses Chrome's `--dump-dom` mode, which waits for `DOMContentLoaded`. Google Docs is a SPA that loads its content asynchronously via JavaScript after the initial page load, so `--dump-dom` times out every time:

```
DEBUG launching headless Chrome for DOM capture
  args=["--headless=new", "--dump-dom", "--timeout=30000",
        "--virtual-time-budget=8000", ...]
WARN  real-browser Google Docs capture failed; falling back to editor HTTP fetch
  error=Browser error: Timed out waiting for headless Chrome to render
```

The `--dump-dom` approach fundamentally cannot work for SPAs like Google Docs. The fix should use CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) to:
1. Navigate to the page
2. Wait for `DOCS_modelChunk` to appear in the JS context
3. Extract the model data via `Runtime.evaluate`

This is exactly what the JS version does successfully with Playwright. The Rust version has `browser-commander` as a dependency which supports CDP — it should use it.

### Full debug log

```
DEBUG starting capture url=.../edit format=archive capture=browser
DEBUG selected Google Docs capture method method=BrowserModel
DEBUG capturing Google Doc editor model with a real browser
INFO  Rendering HTML for URL: .../edit
DEBUG launching headless Chrome for DOM capture
  chrome=/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome
  args=["--headless=new", "--disable-gpu", "--disable-extensions",
        "--disable-dev-shm-usage", "--dump-dom", "--timeout=30000",
        "--virtual-time-budget=8000", "--run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw",
        "--window-size=1280,800", ".../edit"]
WARN  real-browser Google Docs capture failed; falling back to editor HTTP fetch
  error=Browser error: Timed out waiting for headless Chrome to render .../edit
INFO  Fetching HTML from URL: .../edit
INFO  Successfully fetched HTML (432462 bytes)
DEBUG fetched Google Docs editor HTML through HTTP fallback
DEBUG extracted Google Docs editor model chunks chunks=2
INFO  parsed Google Docs editor model chunks=2 cid_urls=4 blocks=121 tables=5 images=26 text_bytes=3323
```

The fallback to HTTP fetch works and extracts the model, but this means `--capture browser` never actually uses a browser for Google Docs. The HTTP fallback should be the `--capture api` path — browser capture must use a real browser or report a clear error.

## Tables have extra empty columns (both Rust and JS browser)

All tables are rendered with ghost empty columns between real columns:

**Expected (3 columns):**
```markdown
| Feature | Supported | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bold | Yes | Using double asterisks |
```

**Actual (5 columns):**
```markdown
| Feature |  | Supported |  | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bold |  | Yes |  | Using double asterisks |
```

This affects all tables in the document. The root cause needs to be found and fixed — likely the `DOCS_modelChunk` table parser is inserting an extra cell boundary between each real cell.

## Rust browser: images not downloaded (0/4)

The Rust browser capture extracts `docs-images-rt` URLs correctly but does not download them to the `images/` directory in archive mode:

```markdown
![Blue rectangle](https://docs.google.com/docs-images-rt/ABaEjg1y9qE4...=s2048)
```

The JS version downloads these to `images/image-01.png` etc. The Rust version should do the same in archive mode.

## Nested ordered sub-lists rendered as bullets (JS) or wrong nesting (both)

**Source:**
```markdown
1.  Parent item 1
    1.  Child item 1.1
    2.  Child item 1.2
```

**JS browser output** (numbered sub-items become bullets):
```markdown
1. Parent item 1
  - Child item 1.1
  - Child item 1.2
```

**Rust browser output** (correct numbers but nesting flattened):
```markdown
1. Parent item 1
  1. Child item 1.1
  2. Child item 1.2
```

Both need to preserve the original ordered list structure with proper nesting.

## Empty table cell positions shifted

**Source:**
```markdown
| A | B | C |
|---|---|---|
|   | x |   |
| y |   | z |
```

**Actual (cells in wrong columns):**
```markdown
| A |  | B |  | C |
|  | x |  |  |  |
| y |  |  | z |  |
```

The `x` should be in column B, but it appears in a ghost column. Combined with the extra-columns bug, cell positions become unpredictable.

## Nested list extra blank lines (both)

Blank lines inserted between nested list children, breaking list continuity:

```markdown
- Parent item 1

  - Child item 1a

  - Child item 1b
```

Should be:
```markdown
- Parent item 1
  - Child item 1a
  - Child item 1b
```

## Summary of all remaining issues

| # | Issue | Rust | JS | Priority |
|---|-------|------|-----|----------|
| 1 | **Browser capture times out on Google Docs** — uses `--dump-dom` instead of CDP | ❌ Always fails | ✅ Works | **Critical** |
| 2 | **Tables have ghost empty columns** | ❌ | ❌ | High |
| 3 | **Images not downloaded in archive mode** | ❌ 0/4 | ✅ 4/4 | High |
| 4 | **Nested ordered sub-lists** wrong type or nesting | Partial | ❌ bullets | Medium |
| 5 | **Empty table cell positions shifted** | ❌ | ❌ | Medium |
| 6 | **Extra blank lines in nested lists** | ❌ | ❌ | Low |

All of these need root causes identified and fixed. The test document at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1f5zI2xOFpKa90v0GjamO_t7lqSdzMlaM/edit and reference markdown at https://gist.github.com/konard/f9533797242666c03097440fd3e30ad5 should be used to validate each fix.

## Related issues

- #90 — Reference test document
- #92 — Previous remaining issues (partially addressed)
- #96 — Previous version test results
- #80 — Original Rust browser capture issue

## Applies to

- [x] Rust CLI (v0.3.4)
- [x] JavaScript CLI (v1.7.12)

title: Fix broken JS release version-specific badge and normalize release titles
body:
## Summary

Closes #98.

**Primary bug:** JavaScript release tag pages showed a "404: badge not found" SVG instead of a version-specific npm badge. `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` was called with the full tag (for example `js-v1.7.12`), stripped only a leading `v`, and interpolated the rest directly into `https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-<tag>-blue.svg`. shields.io's `/badge/label-message-color` path uses `-` as a field separator, so the extra hyphens in `js-v1.7.12` broke the URL.

**Also addressed:**
- Release titles now read `[JavaScript] v<version>` / `[Rust] v<version>` instead of `JS v<version>` / `Rust v<version>`, as requested in the issue.
- All 12 already-published releases (4 broken JS + 8 Rust) have been repaired in place via a new one-shot script, so the GitHub Releases page no longer shows any broken badges or pre-fix titles.

## Root cause

`scripts/format-release-notes.mjs:191` (before):
```js
const versionWithoutV = version.replace(/^v/, '');
```

With `version === 'js-v1.7.12'`, `versionWithoutV` remained `js-v1.7.12`, producing `/badge/npm-js-v1.7.12-blue.svg`. shields.io responded with an SVG whose text read `404: badge not found`.

Fix:
```js
const versionWithoutV = version.replace(/^[a-z]+-/i, '').replace(/^v/i, '');
```

## Before / after

Broken badge (`/badge/npm-js-v1.7.12-blue.svg`): renders `404: badge not found`.

![before](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/issue-98-c765b5595cf4/docs/case-studies/issue-98/reference/broken-badge-before.svg?raw=true)

Fixed badge (`/badge/npm-1.7.12-blue.svg`): renders `npm: 1.7.12`.

![after](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/issue-98-c765b5595cf4/docs/case-studies/issue-98/reference/fixed-badge-after.svg?raw=true)

Live release after the retroactive repair: https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/releases/tag/js-v1.7.12

## Changes

| Commit | What |
| --- | --- |
| `fix(release): strip language prefix from shields.io badge URL` | `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` normalizes `js-v<version>` / `rust-v<version>` / `v<version>` to a bare semver before interpolation. Adds `experiments/test-release-badge-encoding.mjs` as a standalone regression test. |
| `feat(release): use [JavaScript] and [Rust] prefixes in release titles` | `scripts/create-github-release.mjs` and `scripts/rust-create-github-release.mjs` now publish `[JavaScript] v<version>` / `[Rust] v<version>`. |
| `chore(release): add one-shot repair for already-published release bodies` | Idempotent repair script `scripts/fix-existing-release-badges.mjs`. Supports `--dry-run`. Already run once against the repo's 12 pre-fix releases. |
| `docs(case-study): document issue #98 badge investigation` | `docs/case-studies/issue-98/` with timeline, requirements table, root cause, preserved data, verification steps, and upstream follow-up notes. |

## Upstream follow-up

`link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` ships the same latent `replace(/^v/, '')` logic. The template repo itself does not use a `js-v` tag prefix, so the bug does not manifest there - but downstream consumers that tag per-language (like this repo) will hit it. The `link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` uses the dynamic `/crates/v/<name>` shields endpoint and sidesteps the issue entirely. Plan and reproduction steps for an upstream report are documented in `docs/case-studies/issue-98/README.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] Regression test: `node experiments/test-release-badge-encoding.mjs` passes.
- [x] `cd js && npm run lint` reports 0 errors (only pre-existing warnings).
- [x] `cd js && npm run format:check` is clean.
- [x] All modified scripts pass `node --check` syntax validation.
- [x] Dry-run of `scripts/fix-existing-release-badges.mjs` lists exactly the 12 releases that need updating.
- [x] After running the repair script live: `curl -sS https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-1.7.12-blue.svg` renders `aria-label="npm: 1.7.12"`; `gh release view js-v1.7.12` returns `"name":"[JavaScript] v1.7.12"` and a fixed badge URL.

title: Fix Google Docs capture regressions for issue 96
body:
## Summary

- Addresses #96 by hardening Rust Google Docs browser-model capture: Chrome gets a bounded diagnostic attempt, timed-out Chrome children are killed on drop, and the model path falls back to editor HTML when `--dump-dom` does not return.
- Avoids the Windows hosted-runner Google Docs browser-model hang by using the editor HTML model fallback directly on Windows and bounding that HTTP fallback.
- Fixes model markdown regressions in JS and Rust: duplicate empty table columns, same-list joining, multi-paragraph blockquote continuation, nested bold/italic marker balancing, and final trailing newline.

title: Fix Rust release race with concurrent JS release (issue #94)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #94 — the Rust release workflow failed with `! [rejected] main -> main (non-fast-forward)` in [run 24686173280](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/24686173280/job/72197673668) because the JS release workflow auto-bumped `1.7.10` and pushed to `main` first, while the Rust workflow tried to push `0.3.3` on top of the now-stale local `4a3dc43…`. All downstream Rust steps (crates.io publish, GitHub Release) were skipped, so `rust/src/browser.rs` + `rust/src/gdocs.rs` changes from PR #93 never made it to crates.io.

## Root cause

Both `.github/workflows/js.yml` and `.github/workflows/rust.yml` auto-bump on the same push-to-`main` event. Each workflow has its own per-workflow concurrency group (`${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}`), so they run in parallel — they must, since JS needs its own npm OIDC context. Whichever auto-bump finishes first wins; the other's inline `git push origin main` fails with non-fast-forward and the whole release job aborts.

Full timeline, log excerpts, and upstream-template comparison in [`docs/case-studies/issue-94/README.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-94/README.md).

## Fix

New shared helper `scripts/safe-git-push.mjs`:
- `git fetch origin <branch>` up front, rebase if local diverges
- Up to `--max-attempts` (default 5) `git push` attempts
- Between attempts, `git pull --rebase origin <branch>` to absorb concurrent pushes
- Fails fast on non-retriable errors (auth, hook rejection) instead of looping
- `--verbose` / `DEBUG` prints remotes, HEADs, and full push stderr (R6)

All four touch points now go through it:
- `.github/workflows/rust.yml` — auto-bump step
- `.github/workflows/js.yml` — auto-bump step
- `scripts/rust-version-and-commit.mjs` — manual/instant Rust release
- `scripts/version-and-commit.mjs` — manual/instant JS release

## Test plan

- [x] `experiments/test-safe-git-push.mjs` — reproduces the race locally (two clones commit in parallel, one pushes first; the script under test rebases and retries on the loser). Control assertion verifies a raw `git push` still fails with "non-fast-forward".
- [x] `npm run lint` — no new errors
- [x] `npm run format:check` — passes
- [x] Existing Jest suites pass (`publish-verification` etc.)
- [ ] On merge, next JS+Rust concurrent release on `main` publishes both npm and crates.io without non-fast-forward (validates in production)

## Requirements coverage (from issue)

- R1 (root cause): documented in case-study README
- R2 (compare vs upstream templates): `docs/case-studies/issue-94/upstream-templates/` + findings in README
- R3/R4 (case study + timeline): `docs/case-studies/issue-94/`
- R5 (upstream issue): drafted in `docs/case-studies/issue-94/proposed-upstream-issue.md` (to be filed against the link-foundation templates)
- R6 (debug/verbose): `--verbose` flag on `safe-git-push.mjs`

## Reproduction

```bash
node experiments/test-safe-git-push.mjs
# Sandbox: /tmp/safe-git-push-…
# A pushed OK
# Control reproduced the non-fast-forward rejection as expected.
# PASS: safe-git-push.mjs recovered from the race.
```

body:
## Summary

Testing both CLIs against the reference test document (#90) reveals remaining issues across all capture modes. JS `--capture browser` is now the best mode but still has gaps; Rust browser extracts the model but doesn't use it for markdown generation; both API modes lose formatting.

**Test document:** https://docs.google.com/document/d/1f5zI2xOFpKa90v0GjamO_t7lqSdzMlaM/edit
**Reference files:** https://gist.github.com/konard/f9533797242666c03097440fd3e30ad5

## Current state per mode

### JS `--capture browser` (v1.7.9) — best mode, needs fixes

Now preserves headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, blockquotes, lists, links, images, and nested formatting. Remaining issues:

| Feature | Issue |
|---------|-------|
| **Tables** | Multi-column tables collapsed to single-column (`\| A \|` instead of `\| A \| B \| C \|`) |
| **Ordered list numbering** | All items numbered `1.` instead of sequential `1. 2. 3.` |
| **List item spacing** | Extra blank lines between list items |
| **Images** | Extracted via `docs-images-rt` URLs (working), but not downloaded to local `images/` directory — should be downloaded in archive mode |

### Rust `--capture browser` (v0.3.2) — model extracted, markdown generation incomplete

The model is now correctly extracted (`DOCS_modelChunk` parsed: 121 blocks, 5 tables, 4 CID URLs). But the markdown output is plain text with no formatting applied:

| Feature | Issue |
|---------|-------|
| **All formatting** | Bold, italic, strikethrough not applied despite style data being in the model |
| **Headings** | Not generated — all heading levels rendered as plain text |
| **Blockquotes** | Not generated |
| **Lists** | Not generated — items rendered as plain paragraphs |
| **Links** | Not generated — URL data present in model but not output |
| **Tables** | Collapsed to single-column |
| **Images** | Show as `*` placeholder — CID-to-URL mapping extracted (4 URLs found) but images not downloaded or linked |
| **Horizontal rules** | Rendered as single `-` character instead of `---` |

The Rust browser output is currently identical to JS v1.7.8 browser output (before JS got its formatting fixes). The model data is there — it just needs to be used during markdown generation.

### Both `--capture api` (Rust v0.3.2 / JS v1.7.9) — formatting lost in HTML→markdown conversion

Both use `/export?format=html` which returns HTML with inline styles, but the HTML→markdown converter doesn't map them:

| Feature | Issue |
|---------|-------|
| **Bold/italic/strikethrough** | Present in HTML as `<span style="font-weight:700">` etc. but stripped during conversion |
| **Headings** | Rust: converted to underline-style with empty `[]()` anchors prepended. JS: heading numbers escaped (`1\.` instead of `1.`) |
| **Blockquotes** | `>` prefix lost — rendered as plain paragraphs |
| **Links** | Wrapped in Google redirect URLs (`google.com/url?q=...`) instead of direct URLs |
| **` ` entities** | Not decoded — appear as raw ` ` in markdown output |
| **Nested lists** | Partially flattened |

## Expected behavior

All modes should produce markdown that matches the reference `markdown-test-document.md` as closely as possible. The reference document covers 14 feature categories:

1. Headings (H1–H6)
2. Inline formatting (bold, italic, strikethrough)
3. Paragraphs
4. Blockquotes
5. Unordered lists (nested 3 levels)
6. Ordered lists (nested 3 levels)
7. Mixed lists
8. Tables (simple, aligned, formatted content)
9. Links
10. Images (4 embedded PNGs)
11. Horizontal rules
12. Special characters & emoji
13. Nested formatting edge cases
14. Empty/minimal table cells

## Priority order

1. **Rust browser markdown generation** — the hard part (model extraction) is done; applying formatting, headings, lists, blockquotes, links, images, and tables from the parsed model data would bring it to parity with JS browser
2. **JS browser tables** — fix multi-column table rendering (currently single-column)
3. **JS browser ordered list numbering** — sequential numbers instead of all `1.`
4. **JS browser image downloading** — download `docs-images-rt` images to local `images/` in archive mode
5. **API mode formatting** — map inline styles from Google export HTML to markdown (bold, italic, strikethrough, headings, blockquotes)
6. **API mode link unwrapping** — strip Google redirect wrapper from URLs

title: fix(js): add js- prefix to tags/releases to match Rust convention
body:
## Summary

- `scripts/create-github-release.mjs`: tag changed from `v<version>` → `js-v<version>`; release name changed from bare version number → `JS v<version>`
- `scripts/format-github-release.mjs`: tag changed from `v<version>` → `js-v<version>` so the formatter can find the correct release
- Added case study in `docs/case-studies/issue-88/ANALYSIS.md`

Fixes #88.

## Root Cause

JS GitHub releases used `v<version>` tags (e.g., `v1.7.8`) while Rust releases used `rust-v<version>` (e.g., `rust-v0.3.2`). Both languages live in the same repo so tags need a language prefix to be unambiguous.

The Rust scripts already had `rust-v${version}` hardcoded in `scripts/rust-create-github-release.mjs` (line 67). The JS equivalent (`scripts/create-github-release.mjs`) was missing the analogous `js-` prefix.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `scripts/create-github-release.mjs` | Tag: `v${version}` → `js-v${version}`; Name: `version` → `JS v${version}` |
| `scripts/format-github-release.mjs` | Tag: `v${version}` → `js-v${version}` |
| `docs/case-studies/issue-88/ANALYSIS.md` | New case study file |

The JS template (`link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`) has the same bug. Filed as: https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/38

title: Add article content selectors for Habr capture

## Summary

Fixes #76 by adding explicit article/content selector support for Markdown conversion in both JS and Rust implementations.

- Adds `contentSelector` / `bodySelector` support to JavaScript enhanced conversion, CLI, and `/markdown` endpoint.
- Adds `content_selector` / `body_selector` support to Rust enhanced conversion, CLI, and `/markdown` endpoint.

- Adds Habr-shaped regression tests that verify nav/search/write links are excluded while the article title and body remain.
- Adds JS patch changeset; Rust crate version remains on `0.3.2` (bumped earlier).
- Merges latest `main` (Habr archive markdown compatibility controls) and fixes a `const $` reassignment bug introduced by the first draft.

## Reproduction

Before this change, capturing `https://habr.com/en/articles/895896/` as Markdown converted the whole page and included Habr navigation, search/login links, and article page chrome before the article content.

## Expected vs. actual after the fix

With `--content-selector article --body-selector .article-formatted-body`, the resulting Markdown starts at the article title and body content:

```markdown
# The Links Theory 0.0.2

Last April 1st, as you might have guessed, ...
```

## Verification

- `cargo check` passes.
