title: fix(rust): launch browser capture for --capture browser
body:
## Summary

Fixes #80.

- Wires the Rust CLI `--capture browser` flag through `render_html` for normal markdown / archive / html capture paths so the flag actually launches a headless browser instead of falling back to `fetch_html`.
- Keeps `--capture api` as the direct HTTP fetch path for non-Google-Docs URLs.
- Implements real PNG screenshot capture in `capture_screenshot` via the same headless Chrome subprocess used by `render_html`.
- Adds Rust integration tests that validate:
  - `render_html` executes page JavaScript against a local fixture,
  - `capture_screenshot` returns real PNG bytes,
  - `web-capture <url> --capture browser --format markdown -o -` outputs browser-rendered content instead of server HTML.

## Context

Main has advanced significantly since this branch was opened:
- PR #91 (issue #90) introduced the real headless Chrome `render_html` implementation and the Google Docs browser-model capture path.
- PR #93 (issue #92) shipped the Google Docs markdown parity fixes (R1-R6).

This branch now merges `main` and keeps only the remaining gap for issue #80: routing `--capture browser` through `render_html` for non-Google-Docs URLs (the `capture_html_content` helper in `rust/src/main.rs`) and turning the `capture_screenshot` stub into a working Chrome subprocess call.

The earlier chromiumoxide-based rewrite of `browser.rs` from this branch was dropped in favor of main's simpler `--dump-dom` / `--screenshot` subprocess approach, which is already shipping in v0.3.2. `chromiumoxide` and `futures` direct dependencies are removed.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, `--capture browser` against an ordinary URL silently routed through `fetch_html` in `capture_url`, so JavaScript-mutated DOM content was never returned. `capture_screenshot` always returned a `ScreenshotError` stub.

The new integration tests start a local HTTP fixture that mutates its DOM with JavaScript after load and assert that the rendered HTML, markdown, and screenshot PNG bytes reflect the post-render state. The tests skip if no Chrome/Chromium is on PATH.

## Validation

Local runs (headless Chrome on PATH):

- `cd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cd rust && RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — 0 warnings.
- `cd rust && WEB_CAPTURE_BROWSER_WAIT_MS=100 cargo test --all-features` — 167 tests pass (including all 5 browser integration tests).
- `cd js && npm run lint` — 0 errors.
- `cd js && npm run format:check` — clean.
- `cd js && NODE_OPTIONS='--experimental-vm-modules' npx jest --testPathIgnorePatterns="docker.test.js" --testPathIgnorePatterns="gdocs-public-doc"` — 276 tests pass.

title: fix(js): fall back for Google Docs browser capture
body:
## Summary

Fixes #81.

Adds a safety-net fallback for `--capture browser` on Google Docs: when the editor page does not expose `DOCS_modelChunk` data, the JS CLI now warns and falls back to the Google Docs public export pipeline instead of failing or returning a lossy capture. Archive fallback reuses `fetchGoogleDocAsArchive`, so embedded base64 images are still extracted into the archive.

This complements the browser-model improvements from #93 (issue #92 R1–R6): when the model is available (the typical case) we still use it with all the formatting fixes; this PR only kicks in as a lossless fallback when the model is unreachable.

## Changes

- `js/src/gdocs-fallback.js` (new) — houses `captureGoogleDocWithBrowserOrFallback`, `fetchGoogleDocByExportFormat`, `isGoogleDocsBrowserModelUnavailableError`, and `googleDocsBrowserModelUnavailableError`. Kept in its own module so `js/src/gdocs.js` stays under the 1500-line lint limit.
- `js/src/gdocs.js` — throws the sentinel `googleDocsBrowserModelUnavailableError` when `blocks.length === 0`, re-exports the fallback helpers, and exposes thin wrappers that inject sibling fetchers.
- `js/bin/web-capture.js` — calls `captureGoogleDocWithBrowserOrFallback`; archive mode localizes model images when the browser-model path succeeds, and uses the export archive result directly when fallback kicks in.
- `js/tests/unit/gdocs.test.js` — adds `captureGoogleDocWithBrowserOrFallback (issue #81)`, simulating zero model chunks and verifying archive fallback preserves an embedded image.
- `js/.changeset/gdocs-browser-export-fallback.md` — patch changeset.

## Reproduction

Before this change, a Google Docs `/edit` page that exposes no `DOCS_modelChunk` data caused the browser-model path to throw `Google Docs editor page did not expose DOCS_modelChunk data`, leaving browser capture unable to preserve content or images. The new unit test reproduces that state with a fake browser returning zero model chunks and a mocked Google Docs HTML export response with an embedded image.

## Verification

- `cd js && npm run lint` — 0 errors
- `cd js && npm run format:check` — clean
- `cd js && npm run check:duplication` — clean
- `cd js && npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/unit/gdocs.test.js` — 55/55 pass (includes the new fallback test and the merged R5/R6 tests from #93)
- `cd js && npm test -- --testPathIgnorePatterns=tests/e2e/docker.test.js` — 295/295 pass
- `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` — passed

Docker E2E not run locally (no `docker` binary); CI runs it.

title: JS: --capture browser on Google Docs drops all images and loses content
body: ## Bug When using `--capture browser` with the JavaScript CLI on Google Docs URLs, the output loses all images and a significant portion of text content compared to `--capture api`. ## Steps to reproduce ```bash # JS v1.7.6 (internal 0.3.0) web-capture "https://docs.google.com/document/d//edit" --capture api -f archive -o doc-api.zip --engine playwright web-capture "https://docs.google.com/document/d//edit" --capture browser -f archive -o doc-browser.zip --engine playwright ``` ## Expected behavior `--capture browser` should either: 1. Extract meaningful content from the Google Docs page (e.g., via `DOCS_modelChunk` interception as proposed in #72), or 2. Fall back to the export API with a warning, preserving images and content ## Actual behavior `--capture browser` navigates to the `/edit` page, but Google Docs uses canvas-based rendering with no DOM content. The result: - **All images are lost** (0 images vs 30-37 with `--capture api`) - **Content is drastically reduced** (8-11 KB vs 19-23 KB) - **Table structure is lost or degraded** ### Test results (Doc 1 — tables with images) | Capture flag | Lines | Size | Images | |-------------|-------|------|--------| | `--capture api` | 327 | 19,257 bytes | 37 | | `--capture browser` | 290 | 10,947 bytes | **0** | ### Test results (Doc 2 — tables with images and links) | Capture flag | Lines | Size | Images | |-------------|-------|------|--------| | `--capture api` | 10 | 23,359 bytes | 30 | | `--capture browser` | 124 | 8,120 bytes | **0** | ## Tested with - `@link-assistant/web-capture` v1.7.6 (internal 0.3.0) - `--engine playwright` - Two different public Google Docs with tables, images, and links - Archive format ## Root cause Google Docs `/edit` page renders content via `` — there is no HTML DOM with text or `` elements for the browser capture to extract. The JS CLI correctly launches a browser (unlike the Rust version, see #80), but the resulting page has no extractable DOM content. ## Possible solutions 1. **Short-term**: When `--capture browser` detects a Google Docs URL and finds no meaningful DOM content, fall back to `--capture api` with a warning 2. **Long-term**: Implement `DOCS_modelChunk` interception as described in #72 to extract the full document model from the `/edit` page

title: Rust: --capture browser does not launch a browser, produces identical output to --capture api
body:
## Bug

The Rust CLI's `--capture browser` flag does not actually launch a headless browser. It fetches HTML via HTTP requests identically to `--capture api`.

## Steps to reproduce

Capture any Google Doc in archive mode with both methods:

```bash
# Rust v0.3.1
web-capture "https://docs.google.com/document/d/<DOC_ID>/edit" --capture api --archive -o doc-api.zip --verbose
web-capture "https://docs.google.com/document/d/<DOC_ID>/edit" --capture browser --archive -o doc-browser.zip --verbose
```

## Expected behavior

`--capture browser` should launch a headless browser (Chromium via `browser-commander`) and render the page, producing output that reflects browser-rendered content.

## Actual behavior

Both commands produce **byte-identical** output (same markdown size, same image count, same content). The only differences are Google's rotating `ust`/`usg` URL signature parameters in links, which change on every request regardless of method.

The verbose logs confirm no browser is launched — both show:
```
INFO web_capture::html: Fetching HTML from URL: ...
INFO web_capture::markdown: Converting HTML to Markdown
```

For Google Docs specifically, both modes route through `/export?format=html`.

## Tested with

- Rust `web-capture` v0.3.1
- Two different public Google Docs with tables, images, and links
- Archive format with markdown

## Test results

| Capture flag | Lines | Size | Images |
|-------------|-------|------|--------|
| `--capture api` | 302 | 19,331 bytes | 37 |
| `--capture browser` | 302 | 19,331 bytes | 37 |

Output is identical in both cases.

## Impact

The `--capture browser` flag is effectively a no-op in the Rust version. Users who explicitly request browser capture (e.g., for JavaScript-rendered pages or to get faithful Google Docs rendering per #72) silently get an HTTP fetch instead.

title: JavaScript CLI --version reports the caller package version
body:
## Problem

When the JavaScript CLI is run from another npm project, `web-capture --version` reports the caller project's package version instead of @link-assistant/web-capture's package version.

This made release validation confusing while updating link-foundation/meta-theory#10 to the published web-capture package.

## Versions tested

- @link-assistant/web-capture installed version: 1.7.6
- Caller project package version: 1.0.0
- Node: 20.20.2
- Date tested: 2026-04-16

## Reproduction

From a project whose package.json has `"version": "1.0.0"` and depends on `@link-assistant/web-capture@1.7.6`:

```bash
npx web-capture --version
```

## Actual result

```text
1.0.0
```

## Expected result

```text
1.7.6
```

## Likely cause

The yargs `.version()` call appears to infer version from the current working directory package.json rather than the web-capture package.json.

## Suggested fix

Read the version from web-capture's own package.json and pass it explicitly to yargs, e.g. `.version(packageVersion)`.

title: Habr markdown conversion drifts from meta-theory archive format
body:
## Problem

After updating link-foundation/meta-theory#10 to the published @link-assistant/web-capture 1.7.6 package and scoping Habr pages to article-only HTML, generated markdown still differs from the existing meta-theory archives in ways that are not just volatile metadata.

## Versions tested

- JavaScript package: @link-assistant/web-capture 1.7.6
- Downstream repository: link-foundation/meta-theory pull request 56
- Date tested: 2026-04-16

## Reproduction outline

In meta-theory, render https://habr.com/en/articles/895896/ with Playwright, pass only `article h1` + `.article-formatted-body` to `convertHtmlToMarkdownEnhanced()`, and assemble metadata with `formatMetadataBlock()`, `formatFooterBlock()`, and `postProcessMarkdown()`.

Compare the generated markdown with `archive/0.0.2/article.md`.

## Actual differences observed

Examples of non-volatile drift:

1. Figure references stay as remote Habr URLs after article conversion:

```markdown
![...](https://habrastorage.org/r/w1560/getpro/habr/upload_files/....png "Figure 1...")
```

The archive uses stable local figure paths:

```markdown
![Figure 1](images/figure-1.png)
```

The current `localizeImages()` helper would generate `image-01.png` style names, not the existing figure-numbered archive names.

2. Some code blocks lose line breaks. A block that should remain multiline becomes collapsed, for example:

```markdown
L = { 1 , 2 }L × L = { (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 2),}
```

3. Formula output and escaping differ from the archive, for example `$\mathbf{...}$` and ` \\to L^2$` forms differ from the existing markdown style.

4. Typography/link escaping differs broadly enough that exact archive comparison is noisy even after ignoring volatile view counts.

## Expected result

web-capture should provide enough Habr conversion/localization controls for downstream projects to reproduce previous archive-compatible output without reimplementing the converter locally.

At minimum, meta-theory needs options or helpers for:

- stable figure-numbered local paths based on Habr figure captions
- preserving line breaks inside Habr code blocks
- stable LaTeX/formula markdown compatible with existing archives
- documented post-processing options for typography normalization and markdown escaping

## Suggested fix

Add a Habr article fixture test based on representative saved HTML and compare the generated markdown to an expected fixture. The fixture should include formulas, figures, figure captions, and code blocks with line breaks.

title: Rust markdown capture is not feature-parity with JavaScript for Habr formulas and formatting
body: ## Problem The published Rust CLI advertises article-relevant options such as `--extract-latex`, `--extract-metadata`, `--post-process`, and `--detect-code-language`, but its markdown output is not feature-parity with the JavaScript package for Habr articles. This was found while validating link-foundation/meta-theory#10 after the latest JavaScript and Rust releases. ## Versions tested - JavaScript package: @link-assistant/web-capture 1.7.6 - Rust crate/CLI: web-capture 0.3.1 - Date tested: 2026-04-16 ## Reproduction ```bash web-capture https://habr.com/en/articles/895896/ \ --format markdown \ --output rust.md ``` For comparison: ```bash node node_modules/@link-assistant/web-capture/bin/web-capture.js \ https://habr.com/en/articles/895896/ \ --format markdown \ --engine playwright \ --output js.md ``` ## Actual Rust output examples Inline Habr formula images remain raw HTML instead of becoming LaTeX: ```markdown ... everything is serious. ``` Blockquote formulas also remain as raw `` markup. Headings use a different markdown style from JS/meta-theory archives: ```markdown Overview ---------- ``` ## Expected result Rust output should preserve the same article-task feature set as JavaScript for Habr pages: - Habr formula images with `source` attributes become inline/block LaTeX markdown - post-processing behavior is comparable to JavaScript - heading/list/code formatting is stable enough for downstream archive comparison - metadata behavior and article body conversion semantics are documented as equivalent or clearly listed as unsupported ## Why this matters The meta-theory repository archives Habr articles and needs the JavaScript and Rust versions of web-capture to produce comparable article captures. With the current Rust output, formula extraction and formatting are materially different from the JS package and from the archived markdown. ## Suggested fix Port or share the JavaScript Habr LaTeX extraction behavior for `img.formula[source]`, add fixture tests using a Habr-like formula snippet, and add a cross-language parity test for representative Habr article HTML.

title: Habr article captures include page chrome instead of article-only content
body:
## Problem

Capturing a Habr article with the published web-capture CLIs includes Habr navigation, search/login links, ads/page chrome, and article header UI in the markdown output instead of starting at the article content.

This blocks downstream use in link-foundation/meta-theory#10, where archived article markdown must match the previous article-only archives.

## Versions tested

- JavaScript package: @link-assistant/web-capture 1.7.6
- Rust crate/CLI: web-capture 0.3.1
- Date tested: 2026-04-16

## Reproduction

JavaScript:

```bash
node node_modules/@link-assistant/web-capture/bin/web-capture.js \
  https://habr.com/en/articles/895896/ \
  --format markdown \
  --engine playwright \
  --output js.md
```

Rust:

```bash
web-capture https://habr.com/en/articles/895896/ \
  --format markdown \
  --output rust.md
```

## Actual result

The JS output begins with the page title and page chrome, for example:

```markdown
The Links Theory 0.0.2 / Habr

[Habr](https://habr.com/en/feed)[All streams](https://habr.com/en/articles/)

[Search](https://habr.com/en/search/)

[Write a publication](https://habr.com/en/sandbox/start/)
```

The Rust output also includes page chrome after metadata, including Habr navigation and login/search links.

## Expected result

For article capture, markdown should start with the article title and body content, without site navigation, ads, login/search UI, pull-to-refresh text, or page-level chrome:

```markdown
# The Links Theory 0.0.2

Last April 1st, as you might have guessed, ...
```

## Downstream workaround

meta-theory now scopes the rendered Habr page to:

- full `<article>` only for metadata extraction
- `article h1` plus `.article-formatted-body` only for markdown conversion

before calling web-capture conversion helpers.

## Suggested fix

Add an article extraction/selector capability, for example:

- CLI option like `--content-selector article` / `--body-selector .article-formatted-body`
- API option for `convertHtmlToMarkdownEnhanced()` to scope conversion separately from metadata extraction
- or a generic readability/article extraction stage with Habr selectors covered by tests

The key requirement is to keep article metadata extraction available while excluding page chrome from markdown conversion.

title: feat: support Google Docs capture methods
body:
## Summary

Fixes #72.

Adds explicit Google Docs capture-method routing for both CLIs:

- `--capture browser` now uses the editor `/edit` model path instead of the public export endpoint.
- `--capture api` without a token keeps the existing public `/export?format=...` behavior.
- `--capture api` with an API token uses `https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents/<DOC_ID>`.
- JS browser capture installs an init script to intercept `DOCS_modelChunk`, extracts `docs-images-rt` CID mappings, and renders Markdown/HTML/text.
- Rust now exposes matching capture selection, Docs API rendering, and model parsing helpers; its browser-model path parses embedded `/edit` model chunks where available.
- Added issue #72 case-study artifacts under `docs/case-studies/issue-72/`.
- Added gated verbose diagnostics for Google Docs capture. JavaScript uses `log-lazy` behind `--verbose`; Rust uses `tracing` debug output behind `--verbose` or `RUST_LOG`.

This branch also includes current `main` with PR #74, so the removed `/gdocs` HTTP route is not reintroduced.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, Google Docs URL detection ran before the normal browser path, so `--capture browser` still entered the export-based `fetchGoogleDoc*` / `fetch_google_doc*` path. The new regression tests initially failed because the capture-selection/model/API functions did not exist.

The latest review request also required detailed verbose diagnostics. The new logging records method selection, endpoint URLs, response status/content type, body sizes, model chunk counts, CID mapping counts, rendered output sizes, and parsed block/table/image counts without changing default output.

## Tests

- `npm install`
- `npm test -- --runInBand tests/unit/gdocs.test.js`

title: Google Docs: support all capture methods (public export, Docs API, browser DOM)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Feature Request

Currently, Google Docs URLs are always captured via the `/export?format=html` endpoint, regardless of the `--capture` flag value. Even `--capture browser` auto-detects Google Docs URLs and routes them through the export API. This export produces HTML that doesn't always match the live Google Docs editor rendering (row order, cell layout, and content differences in complex table-heavy documents).

## Problem

The `/export?format=html` endpoint is the least faithful representation of a Google Doc. Complex documents with tables containing multiple images per cell, merged cells, or specific formatting can render differently compared to what the user sees in the editor.

Additionally, suggested edit content (images added via suggestions) is **completely stripped** from the export — they don't appear in the exported HTML at all.

## Google Docs URL routes and their data freshness

| Route | Data | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `/edit` | **Fresh, complete** | Contains `DOCS_modelChunk` in `<script>` tags — the full document model including suggested edits. Also contains CID-to-`docs-images-rt` URL mapping. Canvas-based rendering (no DOM content). |
| `/preview` | **May be stale** | For some documents, `/preview` serves outdated content that doesn't reflect recent edits. Also uses canvas rendering. |
| `/pub` | **Requires "Publish to web"** | Only works if the document owner has explicitly published it. Redirects to login otherwise. |
| `/mobilebasic` | **May be stale** | Serves HTML DOM (not canvas), but can show outdated data for some documents. Doesn't include suggested edits. |
| `/export?format=html` | **May be stale, lossy** | Can serve outdated content for some documents. Strips suggested edits, may restructure table rows differently than the editor shows, and re-encodes images as base64. |

**Only the `/edit` route is guaranteed to have fresh, complete data** — including suggested edits and the full document model. The document model (`DOCS_modelChunk`) is embedded in `<script>` tags and contains the same data used to render the canvas.

## Proposed solution

Support three distinct capture methods for Google Docs, selectable by the user:

### 1. Public Export API (current behavior)
- Uses `https://docs.google.com/document/d/<DOC_ID>/export?format=html`
- No authentication required for public documents
- Fastest, but least faithful to editor rendering
- May serve stale content for some documents
- Strips suggested edit content entirely
- Should be the default for `--capture api` when no `--api-token` is provided

### 2. Google Docs REST API (`docs.googleapis.com`)
- Uses `https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents/<DOC_ID>` 
- Returns structured JSON document tree
- Requires OAuth2 authentication (could use `--api-token` or a service account)
- More faithful representation of document structure
- Should be used when `--capture api` is combined with `--api-token`

### 3. Browser DOM capture via `DOCS_modelChunk`
- Navigates to the `/edit` page in a headless browser
- Intercepts `DOCS_modelChunk` from `<script>` tags — the JSON document model
- Extracts CID-to-URL mapping from page scripts (`docs-images-rt` URLs)
- Most faithful to what the user sees in the editor
- **Includes suggested edits** that other methods drop
- `docs-images-rt` image URLs are publicly accessible (no auth needed to download)
- Should be used when `--capture browser` is explicitly specified — currently this flag is ignored for Google Docs URLs

See the [comment below](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/72#issuecomment-4259395295) for a working JavaScript example using [browser-commander](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander).

## Expected behavior

| Flag | No token | With token |
|------|----------|------------|
| `--capture api` | Public export (`/export?format=html`) | Google Docs REST API (`docs.googleapis.com`) |
| `--capture browser` | Browser DOM capture (headless, via `DOCS_modelChunk`) | Browser DOM capture (headless, with auth cookie/session) |

The key change: `--capture browser` should **not** auto-redirect to the export API for Google Docs. It should honor the user's explicit choice and use the browser engine to extract the document model.

## Applies to

- [ ] Rust CLI
- [ ] JavaScript CLI

Both implementations currently auto-detect Google Docs URLs and bypass browser capture.

title: fix(js): accept positional CLI URL arguments
body:
## Summary
Fixes #68.

The JavaScript CLI now accepts capture URLs as positional arguments while keeping yargs strict option validation enabled.

## Root Cause
`js/bin/web-capture.js` enabled `.strict()` without declaring the URL positional argument. yargs rejected `web-capture https://example.com` as an unknown argument before `main()` could run. The code also looked for `config._[0]`, but `lino-arguments` drops yargs' `_` array from the returned config object, so separator-based inputs like `-- https://example.com` could not be recovered there either.

- Declared the default yargs command as `$0 [url]` so strict mode accepts the URL positional.

- Marked `--output` / `-o` with `nargs: 1` so documented stdout output forms like `--output -` keep working under strict mode.
- Added CLI regression tests for positional URLs, `--` separator URLs, unknown-option rejection, and immediate invalid-URL validation.

title: JS CLI: yargs .strict() rejects positional URL argument
body:
## Bug

The JavaScript CLI (`@link-assistant/web-capture` on npm) cannot accept any URL as a positional argument. Every invocation fails with:

```
Unknown argument: https://example.com
```

## Root cause

In `js/bin/web-capture.js`, the yargs configuration uses `.strict()` (line ~228) without defining a positional parameter via `.command()`. In strict mode, yargs rejects any argument that isn't a declared option — including the URL that `main()` expects to find in `config._[0]` (line ~828).

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
bun install -g @link-assistant/web-capture@latest
web-capture https://example.com
# Error: Unknown argument: https://example.com

web-capture https://example.com --format markdown
# Error: Unknown argument: https://example.com

web-capture --capture api --archive zip -- https://example.com
# Error: Missing URL or --serve flag
```

All three forms fail. The CLI is completely non-functional for capture mode.

## Suggested fix

Either:

1. **Remove `.strict()`** — simplest fix, allows positional args through.
2. **Define a positional command** — e.g., `.command('$0 [url]', ...)` so yargs knows about the URL positional.

Option 2 is cleaner as it preserves strict validation for typos in option names.

## Environment

- `@link-assistant/web-capture` npm version: latest (reports `0.3.0` internally)
- Node.js: v20.19.4
- Bun: v1.2.20
- macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)

## Notes

- The `--version` flag reports `0.3.0` even though the npm registry shows versions 1.1.2 → 1.7.2 — the internal version string appears out of sync with the published package version.
- The Rust CLI (`web-capture` on crates.io, v0.3.1) works correctly with the same URLs.

title: fix: handle npm registry lag after successful publish
body:
## Summary
Fixes the JavaScript release failure from issue #66 by separating post-publish verification retries from publish retries.

## Root cause
The failing run published `@link-assistant/web-capture@1.7.1` successfully, but `npm view` still returned a transient `E404` for a few seconds while registry metadata propagated. The old script treated that as a publish failure and retried `npm publish`, which then failed because the same version had already been published.

## Reproduction
1. Run the release flow so `npm publish` succeeds.
2. Make the first one or two `npm view @link-assistant/web-capture@<version> version` checks return transient `E404`.
3. Observe the old script re-run `npm publish` and fail with "You cannot publish over the previously published versions".

## Changes
- retry only the verification step after a successful publish
- poll `npm view` up to 12 times with 5 second spacing before failing verification
- export the verification helper in an import-safe way so it can be regression tested

fix: upgrade Node.js 22→24 for npm OIDC trusted publishing
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: Node.js 22 with upgraded npm 11 fails OIDC token exchange silently, causing `PUT 404 Not Found` on `npm publish` ([npm/cli#8730](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/8730), [npm/cli#8976](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/8976))
- **Fix**: Upgrade to Node.js 24.x which ships with npm 11.x natively and has full OIDC trusted publishing support
- **Diagnostics**: Added `--verbose` flag and OIDC token exchange detection to `publish-to-npm.mjs` so future failures produce actionable error messages instead of misleading "package not found" errors

## Changes

1. **`.github/workflows/js.yml`** — Upgrade `node-version: '22.x'` → `'24.x'` and `actions/setup-node@v4` → `@v6` across all jobs (matching the upstream template)
2. **`.github/workflows/rust.yml`** — Same Node.js and actions version upgrade for consistency
3. **`scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs`** — Add verbose npm publish, OIDC token exchange diagnostics, and differentiated error messages for auth failures vs first-time publish
4. **`docs/case-studies/issue-60/`** — Full case study with timeline, root cause analysis, and references

## Root Cause Details

The npm registry returns `404 Not Found` instead of `401 Unauthorized` when OIDC token exchange fails. On Node 22, even with npm upgraded to 11.4.2, the `.npmrc` generated by `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` interferes with OIDC, causing npm to attempt traditional token auth which silently fails.

Only versions `1.1.2` and `1.4.2` are currently published to npm — all releases since have been affected by this bug.

Evidence: The upstream template repo (`link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`) already uses Node 24.x. Community consensus from 20+ independent reports in npm/cli#8730 confirms Node 24 as the fix.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes with Node 24 on this PR (lint, tests, Docker e2e)
- [ ] After merge to main, release job publishes successfully to npm with OIDC
- [ ] Verbose output in publish logs shows `oidc Successfully retrieved and set token`

title: v0.2.1 archive: markdown image refs point to fabricated URLs; article.html not pretty-printed; HTML-entity decoding incomplete; filenames should be document.* not article.*
body:
## Summary Tested `web-capture v0.2.1` against both test Google Docs. The `--archive zip` output is a **real zip** now (fixes #53), but inside it several new problems make the archive only partially usable. ## Bug A: `article.md` image references point to fabricated, non-existent URLs Every image reference in `article.md` inside the zip looks like: ``` ![](https://docs.google.com/document/d//images/image-01.png "") ``` Problems: 1. `/images/image-01.png` is **not** a real path on `docs.google.com` — these URLs 404. 2. The actual image files are present in the zip at `images/image-01.png` (see Bug B — those are correctly wired up in the HTML). The markdown just doesn't link to them. 3. The end result: after unpacking, the markdown renders zero images locally **and** zero images remotely. Worst of both worlds. Expected: `![](images/image-01.png)` — a relative path matching the HTML's behavior and the zipped file layout. ### Reproduction ```bash web-capture --capture api --archive zip \ "https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0" unzip -d out data/web-capture/.../edit/document.zip grep -c '!\[.*\](images/' out/article.md # → 0 (wrong) grep -c '!\[.*\](https://docs.google.com' out/article.md # → 37 (wrong — fabricated URLs) ``` ## Bug B: image count mismatch between article.md and article.html within the same archive doc2 (`...`): - `article.md` → **29** image references - `article.html` → **30** `` tags - `images/` → **30** files One image is dropped from the markdown entirely. Inside a single archive the two formats should reference the same image set. ## Bug C: `article.html` is not pretty-printed `article.html` inside the archive is written as a single very long line (HTML minified-ish as received from Google's export). Human-readable formatting is expected from a tool that advertises "capture web pages as HTML" as a first-class output. Please pretty-print the HTML (one tag per line, indented) before writing it into the archive and before writing it to standalone `.html` outputs. Use a standard HTML formatter / pretty-printer (both Rust and JS have options: `html5ever` + serializer with indentation, `prettier` on the JS side). ## Bug D: HTML entity decoding of text content is incomplete — outputs should be plain Unicode Both `article.md` and `article.html` contain raw HTML entities (e.g. `&`, ` `, `'`, `"`, numeric entities) instead of the actual Unicode characters. Since the stated default is UTF-8 output, all entity-encoded characters in **text content** should be decoded to Unicode during capture. Clarification of scope: - Decode in: textual content of `article.md`, visible text in `article.html`. - Leave encoded in: HTML attributes where escaping is required for validity (`&` in `href="...?a=1&b=2"`, `<` / `>` / `&` inside `
`/`` blocks where they represent literal code).

This should be **strictly enforced by web-capture itself** — not delegated to downstream tooling — and should be the default for every format (`markdown`, `html`, and the archive contents).

## Bug E: Filenames inside the archive should be `document.*`, not `article.*`

The outer auto-derived filename is `document.zip`. Inside, the contents are `article.md` + `article.html` + `images/`. Pick one. The issue originally asked for `document.md` / `document.html` for consistency, and for a generic name that applies to **all** capture types, not just "articles":

- A captured Google Doc, a captured marketing page, a captured GitHub README, and a captured arbitrary URL are not all "articles" — some are documents, landing pages, dashboards, etc. `document.*` is a neutral generic term that fits all of them.
- The outer filename (`document.zip`) and inner filenames should match: `document.md`, `document.html`, `images/`.
- Same rule applies for non-archive outputs: `./data/web-capture///document.md`, `document.html`, etc. — never `article.*`.

## What works (verified in v0.2.1)

- Real zip container produced (fixes #53 Bug 1).
- Correct `.zip` extension in auto-derived path (fixes #53 Bug 4).
- `images/` directory populated with real PNG/JPG binary files (fixes #53 Bug 2 partially).
- `article.html` image `src` attributes correctly point to relative `images/image-NN.ext` paths — this is the correct pattern; `article.md` just needs to follow the same pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A) `article.md` (renamed to `document.md` per E) image references use relative `images/image-NN.ext` paths, identical to what `article.html` already does.
- [ ] B) Markdown and HTML inside the same archive reference the exact same set of images (same count, same order).
- [ ] C) HTML output (inside archives and standalone) is pretty-printed with indentation by default. Opt-out flag (`--no-pretty-html` / `WEB_CAPTURE_PRETTY_HTML=false`) for users who want minified output.
- [ ] D) HTML entities in text content are decoded to Unicode by default in all output formats. Enforced by web-capture itself.
- [ ] E) Generic filenames throughout: `document.md`, `document.html`, `document.zip` / `document.7z` / etc. No `article.*` anywhere. Applied to both the archive contents and the auto-derived `./data/web-capture/.../` layout.
- [ ] Parity: identical behavior in the JavaScript implementation per the standing parity policy.

## Environment

- `web-capture 0.2.1` (crates.io, installed via `cargo install web-capture --version 0.2.1`)
- macOS Darwin 24.6.0

title: fix(ci): self-healing release pipeline — auto-detect and release accumulated unreleased changes
body:
## Summary

Fixes #56 — PR #54 merged fixes but no release was cut because the release pipeline silently skipped when no version bump was present.

### Root Cause

The Rust release job used `rust-version-check.mjs` which only checked if a git tag `rust-v{version}` existed. Since v0.2.0 was already tagged, the script returned `should_release=false` — it never checked for unreleased commits on main. The JS release job had the same class of problem, gating entirely on changeset file presence.

**Evidence from CI logs** (run 24394459262, lines 7096-7099):
\`\`\`
Current version: 0.2.0
Tag rust-v0.2.0 already exists
Output: should_release=false
\`\`\`

### Solution

Replace git-tag-based / changeset-only gating with **registry-based checks** (crates.io for Rust, npm for JS) plus **unreleased change detection**:

1. **New script `rust-check-release-needed.mjs`**: Checks crates.io (not git tags) as the source of truth. If the version is already published, compares HEAD against the latest release tag for publishable path changes. If found → auto-bump patch version and release.

2. **New script `check-release-needed.mjs`**: Same logic for JS/npm — checks npm registry, then checks for unreleased publishable commits since the last `v*` tag.

3. **New script `check-publishable-changes.mjs`**: PR-time check that warns (via GitHub Actions annotation) when publishable paths change without a version bump or changeset.

4. **Updated workflows**: Both `rust.yml` and `js.yml` release jobs now use the new scripts and include auto-bump steps.

### Decision Tree

\`\`\`
Push to main
├── Check registry (crates.io / npm)
│   ├── Version NOT published → release as-is
│   └── Version IS published
│       ├── Diff HEAD vs last release tag for publishable paths
│       │   ├── Changes found → auto-bump patch → release
│       │   └── No changes → skip (correct)
│       └── No release tag → skip
\`\`\`

### Acceptance Criteria Status

- [x] Push to main with no version bump MUST NOT silently skip — now auto-bumps and releases
- [x] Pipeline detects accumulated unreleased changes (not just last PR) — compares HEAD vs last release tag
- [x] Same logic for both Rust (crates.io) and JS (npm) pipelines
- [x] PR-time check warns when publishable paths change without changeset/version bump

### Template Issues Filed

- [js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#36](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/36) — same gap exists in the JS template (Rust template already has `check-release-needed.rs`)

### Case Study

Full root cause analysis, timeline, and CI logs preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-56/`.

## Test Plan

- [x] All new scripts pass `node --check` syntax validation
- [x] YAML workflows pass `yaml.safe_load()` validation
- [x] Logic test (`experiments/test-release-check-logic.mjs`) passes all 6 scenarios including the exact PR #54 reproduction case
- [ ] CI runs on this PR to verify workflow syntax
- [ ] After merge: verify next push to main with unreleased changes triggers auto-release

## Files Changed

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `scripts/rust-check-release-needed.mjs` | New: crates.io-based release check with unreleased change detection |
| `scripts/check-release-needed.mjs` | New: npm-based release check with unreleased change detection |
| `scripts/check-publishable-changes.mjs` | New: PR-time publishable path warning |
| `.github/workflows/rust.yml` | Updated release job + added publishable-check job |
| `.github/workflows/js.yml` | Updated release job + added publishable-check job |
| `experiments/test-release-check-logic.mjs` | Test script for release decision tree |
| `docs/case-studies/issue-56/` | Case study with CI logs and analysis |

title: CI/CD: PR #54 merged fixes but no release was cut — release pipeline should process any accumulated unreleased changes on every main push
body:
## Summary

PR #54 merged to `main` at 2026-04-14T10:38:43Z with the fixes for #53 (Google Docs archive + image extraction bugs). The CI/CD workflow ran on the merge commit (`8b178a78`) and reported success, but **no new release was published** — neither on crates.io (still at 0.2.0) nor as a GitHub release tag (latest still `rust-v0.2.0` from earlier today, 09:33:46Z, *before* the PR merge).

End users running `cargo install web-capture` still get v0.2.0, which contains the broken `--archive zip` behavior. The fixes are merged but unshipped.

## Root cause

The `Rust Checks and Release` workflow on commit `8b178a78` shows:

| Job | Status |
|---|---|
| Rust - Detect Changes | success |
| **Rust - Instant Release** | **skipped** |
| **Rust - Create Changelog PR** | **skipped** |
| Rust - Lint / Test / Build | success |
| Rust - Release | success (no-op) |

Run: https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/24394459262

Both release-producing jobs (`Instant Release` and `Create Changelog PR`) were skipped because **PR #54 did not include a changeset / version bump** in `rust/Cargo.toml` (still `version = "0.2.0"`). The release pipeline is gated on the presence of a changeset or a version change, so a merge with fix code but no changeset silently produces no release.

This is the same class of problem hit in PRs #41/#43/#45/#47 (all titled "fix CI/CD release pipeline"): the pipeline is too eager to skip.

## Required behavior

The CI/CD pipeline on `main` must be **self-healing** with respect to unreleased commits. On every push to `main`, the release workflow should:

1. Compare the version in `rust/Cargo.toml` (and the JS `package.json`) against the latest **published** version on crates.io / npm.
2. Compare the current `HEAD` against the latest **release tag** on GitHub.
3. If there are commits on `main` since the last release tag **AND** those commits touch publishable paths (`rust/src/**`, `rust/Cargo.toml`, `js/src/**`, `js/bin/**`, `js/package.json`, etc.), then:
   - If no version bump is present, auto-bump the patch version (or open a changelog PR) **without requiring a contributor to remember a changeset**.
   - If a version bump *is* present, cut the release.
4. Never leave `main` in a state where merged fix commits sit unreleased indefinitely because "no changeset was included."

The key invariant: **any main-branch CI/CD run should be able to process accumulated unreleased changes from prior skipped releases**, not just the delta from a single PR. Today's run at 10:38 UTC had PR #54's fixes sitting on main with no release — the very next main-branch CI run should detect that gap and publish.

## Reproduction

1. `cargo info web-capture | grep version` → `0.2.0`
2. `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/link-assistant/web-capture/main/rust/Cargo.toml | grep version` → `0.2.0`
3. `git log rust-v0.2.0..main --oneline` → includes merge commit for PR #54 (`8b178a78`, the #53 fix) plus anything merged after
4. `gh release list` → latest is still `rust-v0.2.0`, tagged *before* the PR merge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A push to `main` with merged code but no bumped version MUST NOT silently skip releasing. Either auto-bump the version on main, or fail the workflow loudly with a clear message so humans notice.
- [ ] The pipeline MUST detect and process **accumulated** unreleased changes (not just the last PR). E.g. if PR #54, PR #X, and PR #Y all merged without version bumps, a later main run must cut one release that covers all of them.
- [ ] Same logic applied to both the Rust release pipeline (crates.io + GitHub release) and the JS release pipeline (npm).
- [ ] Add a CI status check that fails on PR merge if the PR touches publishable code paths but no version bump / changeset is present — so the gap is caught at PR time rather than silently after merge.

## Priority

High. Users following the documented install instruction (`cargo install web-capture`) currently get a version where `--archive zip` produces raw HTML (the exact regression PR #54 fixed). Every hour of delay between merge and release is a bug that's fixed in source but broken in the binary users install.

## Related

- PR #54 (merged, unreleased): https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/54
- Issue #53 (fixed by #54, still reproducible with 0.2.0): https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/53
- Prior release-pipeline fixes: #41, #43, #45, #47

title: fix: Google Docs archive produces real zip, default markdown extracts images
body:
## Summary

Fixes #53 — six bugs in the Google Docs capture path that made `--archive zip` and default markdown mode unusable:

- **Bug 1 & 5**: `--archive zip` wrote raw HTML bytes instead of a real zip archive (both with `-o` and auto-derived paths)
- **Bug 2**: Default markdown mode silently stripped all base64 images from Google Docs (which only has data URIs), producing lossy output with zero images
- **Bug 3**: `WEB_CAPTURE_KEEP_ORIGINAL_LINKS=false` was ignored — images were always stripped on the gdocs path
- **Bug 4**: Auto-derived archive path used `document.archive` instead of `document.zip`

## Root Causes

### Rust (`rust/src/main.rs`)
- `capture_url()` passed `"archive"` as the format to the Google Docs match, but the match only handled `"markdown"` — falling through to the `_` catch-all which wrote raw HTML directly
- The markdown path called `strip_base64_images()` when `!embed_images` (default), discarding all images. It never checked `keep_original_links` and never called `extract_and_save_images()`

### JavaScript (`js/bin/web-capture.js`, `js/src/markdown.js`)
- Same structural bugs: no `"archive"` handling for Google Docs URLs, and markdown mode stripped instead of extracting

## Changes

### Rust
- Added `"archive"` match arm for Google Docs → calls `fetch_google_doc_as_archive()` + `create_archive_zip()`
- Added `"archive"` match arm for regular URLs → uses `extract_base64_to_buffers()` + `create_archive_zip()`
- Fixed markdown mode: extracts base64 images to `images/` dir by default, strips only when `--keep-original-links` is explicitly set
- Uses correct archive extension (`zip`/`7z`/`tar.gz`/`tar`) in auto-derived paths
- Fixed API `/markdown` handler to respect `embedImages` parameter correctly

### JavaScript
- Added `archive`/`zip` format handling for Google Docs URLs using `fetchGoogleDocAsArchive()`
- Fixed markdown mode: extracts base64 images to `images/` dir by default (both gdocs and regular paths)
- Fixed `keepOriginalLinks` logic: only strip when explicitly requested
- Fixed API markdown handler: removed unused `keepOriginalLinks` variable, simplified strip logic

### Tests
- **Rust**: 2 new tests verifying `create_archive_zip` produces valid ZIP with correct contents (article.md, article.html, images/)
- **JS**: 4 new tests verifying the image extraction pipeline (HTML extraction, disk extraction, stripping, buffer extraction)

- [x] `cargo check` — compiles clean
- [x] `cargo test --test unit --test integration` — 85/85 pass

- [x] JS unit tests — 194/200 pass (6 browser.test.js failures are pre-existing env issue)
- [x] ESLint — 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings for function complexity)
- [x] Prettier — formatting verified
- [ ] Manual test with real Google Docs URL: `web-capture --archive zip <gdocs-url>` → should produce a real zip
- [ ] Manual test: `web-capture <gdocs-url>` → should create `document.md` + `images/` directory

title: v0.2.0 bug: --archive zip writes raw HTML for Google Docs; default markdown strips all images
body:
## Summary

Reproduced against `web-capture v0.2.0` (just published to crates.io, installed via `cargo install web-capture --version 0.2.0`). Two related bugs in the Google Docs capture path make it impossible to obtain `markdown + images` either as a directory layout or as an archive.

## Bug 1: `--archive zip` produces raw HTML, not a zip

For any Google Docs URL, every invocation of `--archive zip` writes the raw HTML export bytes to the output path, with no zip container. The CLI logs `Google Doc (archive) saved to: ...zip` but the file is plain HTML.

### Reproduction

```bash
web-capture --capture api --archive zip \
  -o doc1.zip \
  "https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0"

file doc1.zip
# → doc1.zip: HTML document text, ASCII text, with very long lines (65536), with no line terminators

unzip -l doc1.zip
# → End-of-central-directory signature not found.
```

Same result with all of these variants — none produce a real zip:

- `--archive zip` (default format)
- `--format markdown --archive zip`
- `--format md --archive zip`
- without `--capture api` (browser path)
- with `WEB_CAPTURE_KEEP_ORIGINAL_LINKS=false`

The `--archive` flag is parsed and recognized (no error), but on the gdocs code path the archive writer is never invoked — the raw HTML response is written to the output path verbatim.

## Bug 2: Default markdown mode silently discards every image on Google Docs

Without `--embed-images` and without `--archive`, the gdocs path takes the "keep original links" branch. Google Docs HTML exports contain **only** `data:image/...;base64,...` URIs — there are no remote original URLs to preserve. The tool then **strips all images** and writes a markdown file with zero images and no `images/` directory.

### Reproduction

```bash
rm -rf data
web-capture --capture api \
  "https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0"

# stderr:
#   Stripped 37 base64 images (keeping original links)
#   Google Doc Markdown saved to: ./data/web-capture/docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit/document.md

find data -type f
# → only document.md
# → no images/ directory, no image files
```

37 images silently discarded. Markdown references to those images are also dropped, so the output is lossy with no warning beyond a single info-level line.

## Bug 3: `WEB_CAPTURE_KEEP_ORIGINAL_LINKS=false` is honored by the parser but ignored by the gdocs path

```bash
WEB_CAPTURE_KEEP_ORIGINAL_LINKS=false web-capture --capture api \
  "https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0"
# → still prints "Stripped 37 base64 images (keeping original links)"
# → still no images/ directory
```

The flag is parsed (Clap accepts it), but the gdocs branch decides to strip before consulting the flag — or consults a different default. Either way: setting it to `false` does not enable extraction.

Note also that Clap rejects `WEB_CAPTURE_KEEP_ORIGINAL_LINKS=0` with `error: invalid value '0' for '--keep-original-links' [possible values: true, false]`. Env vars for boolean flags should accept `0|1`/`true|false`/`yes|no` — this is what `lino-arguments`' `getenv` boolish parsing gives you, and Clap should be configured to match for parity.

## What works (the only currently usable mode for gdocs)

`--embed-images` produces a self-contained markdown with base64 inline. This is the only v0.2.0 mode that preserves the images at all on the gdocs path.

```bash
web-capture --capture api --embed-images \
  "https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0"
# → ./data/web-capture/.../document.md (2.6 MB, all 37 images inlined as base64)
```

## Required behavior

### For `--archive` (default and explicit)

When `--archive` is set (with or without an explicit format value), the tool must:

1. Default `--format` to `markdown` for the document inside the archive (this is already the CLI default for `--format`, just make sure `--archive` respects it instead of falling back to HTML).
2. **Always** extract images to a separate `images/` folder inside the archive — `--download-images` (or equivalent extraction) must be **on by default in archive mode**, regardless of the `--keep-original-links` / `--embed-images` defaults that apply to plain markdown mode. An archive whose markdown references images that aren't in the archive is useless.
3. Write a real archive container (zip / 7z / tar.gz / tar) with this layout at the root:
   ```
   document.md
   images/
       image-001.png
       image-002.jpg
       ...
   ```
4. For Google Docs base64 data URIs: decode to binary and place under `images/`.
5. For remote `http(s)://` image URLs: download and place under `images/`.

This must work identically through:
- the CLI: `web-capture --archive zip -o out.zip <url>`
- the HTTP API server (`--serve`): e.g. `GET /?url=...&archive=zip` returning `application/zip`.

### For default markdown mode (no `--archive`, no `-o` override)

When the user runs:

```bash
web-capture "https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0"
```

…the result must be a usable directory tree:

```
./data/web-capture/docs.google.com/document/d/<DOC_ID>/edit/
    document.md
    images/
        image-001.png
        ...
```

For Google Docs (which only has base64), the default must be **extract to `images/`**, not strip. "Keep original links" only makes sense for sources where original URLs actually exist; for data URIs it should always fall back to extraction.

### Surface

- `--download-images` / `--no-download-images` (+ `WEB_CAPTURE_DOWNLOAD_IMAGES`) — controls whether remote image URLs are downloaded into `images/`. Default: **true in archive mode**, configurable in plain markdown mode.
- The same logic applies to base64 data URIs (which are always "local" — there's nothing to download, just decode). They should be extracted whenever images are not explicitly being embedded (`--embed-images`).
- Boolean env vars must accept `0|1` and `true|false` and `yes|no` (parity with JS `getenv`).

## Why this matters

Per #48, the whole point of v0.2.0 was "markdown + images as separate files." With the current behavior, on Google Docs URLs (a primary advertised use case):

- Default mode → loses images entirely.
- `--archive zip` → writes raw HTML with a `.zip` extension.
- The only mode that doesn't lose data is `--embed-images`, which is exactly the bloated single-file output #48 was filed to avoid.

## Environment

- `web-capture v0.2.0` (installed via `cargo install web-capture --version 0.2.0`)
- macOS Darwin 24.6.0
- Test URLs:
  - `https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0` (37 images)
  - `https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0`

## Cross-language parity

Per the parity policy on #48, the JavaScript implementation must match: same `--archive` semantics, same `--download-images` default-on-in-archive-mode behavior, same `images/` layout, same env var name and boolish parsing.

title: fix: skip CI tests on non-code file changes using detect-changes job
body:
## Summary

- **Add runtime change detection**: New `scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs` script detects what files actually changed and outputs per-language flags
- **Replace static `paths:` filters**: Both `js.yml` and `rust.yml` workflows now use a `detect-changes` job to gate downstream jobs instead of YAML-level `paths:` filters
- **Per-commit diff instead of full-PR diff**: Uses `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` for PR merge commits (GitHub Actions synthetic merge) to evaluate only what the latest push changed, not the entire PR
- **Skip tests for non-code files**: Files like `.gitkeep`, `.gitignore`, `LICENSE`, markdown docs, and files in `docs/`, `experiments/`, `examples/` folders no longer trigger test runs
- **Add Docker build retry logic**: Both JS and Rust Dockerfiles now retry `apt-get install` up to 3 times to handle transient Debian mirror network errors in CI

Fixes #50

## Root Cause

Two separate issues were causing unnecessary CI runs:

1. **GitHub Actions `paths:` filters** evaluate against **all files changed in the entire PR**, not just the latest commit. When a PR has commits touching `js/**` and a later commit only modifies `.gitkeep`, the JS workflow still runs because the PR as a whole includes `js/**` changes.

2. **The initial detect-changes script** used `git diff base_sha head_sha` for PRs, which gives the **full PR diff** — the same problem as `paths:` filters. Additionally, GitHub Actions checks out a **synthetic merge commit** for `pull_request` events, so even `HEAD^..HEAD` gives the full PR diff (since `HEAD^` is the base branch, not the previous PR commit).

**Evidence**: commit `0e9b6e8c` in PR #49 only modified `.gitkeep` but triggered all 8 CI jobs. Commit `aa262e5` in this PR (a revert touching only `.gitkeep`) also incorrectly triggered all tests.

## Solution

### Per-commit diff via merge commit detection

The key fix detects GitHub Actions' synthetic merge commit and uses `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` instead:
- `HEAD` = synthetic merge commit
- `HEAD^` = base branch (first parent) 
- `HEAD^2` = actual PR head commit (second parent)
- `HEAD^2^` = PR head commit's parent

So `git diff HEAD^2^ HEAD^2` gives the per-commit diff of the latest push — exactly what we need.

For push events (non-merge commits), the regular `HEAD^..HEAD` is used.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs` | New — runtime change detection with merge commit awareness and per-language output flags |
| `.github/workflows/js.yml` | Removed `paths:` filters, added `detect-changes` job, gated jobs on outputs |
| `.github/workflows/rust.yml` | Removed `paths:` filters, added `detect-changes` job, gated jobs on outputs |
| `js/Dockerfile` | Added apt-get install retry loop (3 attempts) for transient network errors |
| `rust/Dockerfile` | Added apt-get install retry loop (3 attempts) for transient network errors |
| `docs/case-studies/issue-50/analysis.md` | Case study with root cause analysis and timeline |
| `experiments/test-detect-changes.mjs` | 19 edge-case tests for detect-code-changes.mjs logic |

### CI verification

**Commit `d87498f`** (changed only `scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs`):
- Rust detect-changes correctly outputs `any-rust-code-changed=false` → all Rust jobs **skipped**
- JS detect-changes correctly outputs `any-js-code-changed=true` (it's a JS script) → JS lint/test **run**
- Changeset check correctly **skipped** (no JS source code changes)

**CI log excerpt** (Rust detect-changes for commit `d87498f`):
```
Merge commit detected (pull_request event)
Comparing HEAD^2^ to HEAD^2 (per-commit diff of PR head)
Changed files:
  scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs
any-rust-code-changed=false
```

## Test plan

- [x] `detect-code-changes.mjs` tested locally — correctly identifies `.gitkeep` as non-code
- [x] Script outputs `any-code-changed=false` for `.gitkeep`-only changes
- [x] Merge commit detection tested with simulated merge commit — `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` gives per-commit diff
- [x] 19 edge-case tests pass in `experiments/test-detect-changes.mjs`
- [x] Rust-only script changes (`scripts/rust-*`) don't trigger JS CI
- [x] CI: Rust jobs correctly skipped when only JS script changed (commit `d87498f`)
- [x] CI: JS lint/test correctly run when JS script changed
- [x] CI: Changeset check correctly skipped for non-source changes

title: Extract images to /images folder by default instead of embedding base64 in markdown, and other issues for Rust and JavaScript versions
body:
## Problem

When capturing a page as markdown (e.g. a Google Doc via `--capture api --format markdown --enhanced`), all images are emitted as `data:image/...;base64,...` URIs inline in the markdown file. This bloats the output file dramatically.

### Reproduction

```
web-capture -f markdown --enhanced --capture api \
  -o document.md \
  "https://docs.google.com/document/d/.../edit?tab=t.0"
```

Result: a single `document.md` of ~2.7 MB where the vast majority of bytes are base64-encoded images inlined into the markdown. A second test doc produced ~6.2 MB of markdown for the same reason.

### Impact

- The markdown file is unreadable in most editors/viewers (lines of base64 hundreds of KB long).
- Diffing, grepping, and version-controlling the markdown is impractical.
- There is no way to hand the images to downstream tooling as real image files.
- Packaging "markdown + images" as an archive currently requires the user to post-process the base64 back into files themselves.

## Proposed behavior

By default, when outputting markdown, `web-capture` should:

1. Decode each embedded image to its original binary (PNG / JPEG / GIF / WebP / SVG — detected from the data URI mime type or magic bytes).
2. Write images as separate files under an `images/` folder next to the markdown output (e.g. `images/001.png`, `images/002.jpg`, ...). Deterministic names (index- or hash-based) are fine.
3. Rewrite the markdown image references to relative paths like `![](images/001.png)`.

When `-o path/to/document.md` is given, the folder should be `path/to/images/`. When writing to stdout, fall back to the current inline behavior (or require `-o` for extraction).

## Opt-in base64

Keep the current inline-base64 behavior available behind a flag for users who specifically want a single self-contained markdown file, e.g.:

```
--embed-images           # opt-in: inline images as base64 data URIs (current default)
--images-dir <DIR>       # override the default "images" folder name/path
--no-extract-images      # alternative spelling, keep everything inline
```

Suggested default: extract to `./images/`. Opt-in to inline.

## Why change the default

The current default optimizes for "single file" at the cost of making the markdown unusable for nearly every normal downstream workflow (reading, diffing, publishing to a static site, feeding to an LLM, etc.). Extracting images is the behavior users almost always want from a "capture page as markdown" tool — see e.g. pandoc's `--extract-media`, monolith, SingleFile-to-md converters, etc.

## Environment

- `web-capture` 0.1.0 (installed via `cargo install web-capture`)
- macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)

title: fix: fallback to CARGO_TOKEN and fail instead of skip when publishing to crates.io
body:
## Summary

Fixes #46

- **Fix token fallback**: `rust-publish-crate.mjs` now resolves the crates.io token from `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (preferred) or `CARGO_TOKEN` (backwards compatibility), matching the convention used across `browser-commander`, `lino-arguments`, `Numbers`, and the `rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`
- **Fail instead of skip**: When neither token is configured, the script now fails with `exit(1)` and a clear `::error::` annotation, instead of silently exiting with code 0 and `published=false`
- **Pre-check crates.io API**: Before attempting `cargo publish`, checks the crates.io API to detect already-published versions (avoids unnecessary publish attempts)
- **Explicit --token flag**: Token is passed explicitly via `cargo publish --token` rather than relying solely on env var detection
- **Auth failure diagnostics**: Detects authentication errors and provides remediation guidance
- **Workflow token fallback**: Both `release` and `instant-release` jobs now pass `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` and `CARGO_TOKEN` with the `||` fallback chain

## Root Cause

The CI log from [run 24332395778](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/24332395778) shows:

```
CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: 
Current version to publish: 0.1.0
CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN not set, skipping publish
Output: published=false
Output: skipped=true
```

The `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret was empty, and the script had no fallback to `CARGO_TOKEN`. It also exited with code 0 (success) instead of failing.

Full analysis in [docs/case-studies/issue-46/README.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/issue-46-74be9b28b867/docs/case-studies/issue-46/README.md).

## Summary

Fixes #44

- **Fix npm publish OIDC error handling**: The `publish-to-npm.mjs` script now fails with a clear error message and detailed manual publish instructions when OIDC trusted publishing returns 404 (not configured on npmjs.org for the `@link-assistant` scope). No token-based fallback — tokens are not used.
- **Update JS dependencies**: `lino-arguments` from `^0.2.5` to `^0.3.0` (latest)
- **Make browser-commander required in Rust**: `browser-commander` `0.9` is now a required dependency (not optional/feature-gated), matching the issue requirement to use it by default in both JavaScript and Rust
- **Enable Rust dependencies**: `lino-arguments` `0.3` added to `Cargo.toml`
- **Align CI/CD workflows with reference repo best practices**:
  - Add `cancel-in-progress: true` to concurrency settings
  - Add `CARGO_TERM_COLOR` and `RUSTFLAGS` environment variables
  - Add cache `restore-keys` for partial cache hits
  - Add `--verbose` flag to Rust test commands
  - Add `cargo package --list --allow-dirty` build verification
  - Add `changelog-pr` manual release mode to Rust workflow
  - Align all Node.js versions to 22.x (matching `engines` field)
  - Add explicit `token` parameter in checkout for release jobs

## Root Cause Analysis

The CI failure in [run 24275913722](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/24275913722) was caused by:

1. **Primary**: npm OIDC trusted publishing not configured for `@link-assistant` scope on npmjs.org. The `npm publish --provenance --access public` command signed provenance successfully but the registry returned `404 Not Found` on the PUT request.
2. **Secondary**: Node.js 22.22.2 on GitHub Actions runners has a broken npm 10.9.7 missing `promise-retry` module ([actions/runner-images#13883](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13883)). The existing fallback logic in `setup-npm.mjs` handles this.

Full analysis in [docs/case-studies/issue-44/README.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/issue-44-5fc8fd3303bb/docs/case-studies/issue-44/README.md).

## Feedback Addressed

- **Removed token-based publish fallback** (per [reviewer feedback](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/45#issuecomment-4234567277)): When OIDC 404 occurs, the script now fails immediately with clear instructions for manual first-time publish and OIDC configuration
- **Made browser-commander non-optional in Rust** (per reviewer feedback): Removed the `browser` feature gate — `browser-commander` is now a required dependency, used by default in both JS and Rust

title: fix: resolve CI/CD release pipeline failure (git show path bug)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #42 — CI/CD release pipeline failure in [run 24262572320](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/24262572320/job/70853245788).

- **Primary fix**: `version-and-commit.mjs` used `git show origin/main:package.json` to check the remote version, but `git show` resolves paths relative to the **repo root**, not the working directory. Since the workflow runs from `js/`, the correct path is `js/package.json`. Fixed by using `git rev-parse --show-prefix` to dynamically resolve the subdirectory prefix.
- **Secondary fix**: Added `npx --yes npm@11 install -g npm@11` as a new fallback in `setup-npm.mjs` for the [Node.js 22.22.2 broken npm issue](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13883), where `npm install -g` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `promise-retry`.
- **Case study**: Added detailed root cause analysis and timeline in `docs/case-studies/issue-42/`.

## Root Cause

The `getVersion('remote')` function in `scripts/version-and-commit.mjs` ran:
```javascript
await $`git show origin/main:package.json`
```

But `git show <ref>:<path>` always uses **repo-root-relative** paths. The script runs from the `js/` subdirectory (via `working-directory: js` in the workflow), so the file is at `js/package.json` in git's tree. This only triggers when remote main has advanced since the CI run started (a race condition between concurrent releases).

The error from CI:
```
fatal: path 'js/package.json' exists, but not 'package.json'
Error: Unexpected end of JSON input
```

## Fix

```javascript
// Before (broken):
const result = await $`git show origin/main:package.json`.run({ capture: true });

// After (fixed):
const prefixResult = await $`git rev-parse --show-prefix`.run({ capture: true });
const prefix = prefixResult.stdout.trim();  // "js/"
const gitPath = `${prefix}package.json`;    // "js/package.json"
const result = await $`git show origin/main:${gitPath}`.run({ capture: true });
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify CI checks pass on this PR
- [ ] After merge, trigger a release and verify `version-and-commit.mjs` handles remote divergence correctly
- [ ] Verify `setup-npm.mjs` npm upgrade succeeds via npx fallback on Node.js 22.22.2 runners

title: fix: repair CI/CD release pipeline for JS npm publish and Rust crates.io
body:
## Summary

Fixes #40 — CI/CD release pipeline was broken for both JavaScript (npm) and Rust (crates.io) publishing.

### Root Causes Found

1. **JS npm publish fails silently** — `changeset publish` was used for publishing but it does not support OIDC trusted publishing for scoped packages (`@link-assistant/web-capture`), returning E404. The error was not caught because `changeset publish` exits with code 0 even on failure.
   - **Evidence**: Only version `1.1.2` exists on npm despite CI reporting success for `1.2.0` and `1.3.0`
   - **Fix**: Replace `changeset publish` with `npm publish --provenance --access public` + post-publish verification

2. **Rust release never triggered** — `rust-version-check.mjs` used `git rev-parse` to check for tags, which gave false positives for non-existent tags (interpreted ambiguous arguments as paths)
   - **Evidence**: CI log shows `fatal: ambiguous argument 'rust-v0.1.0'` followed by `Tag rust-v0.1.0 already exists`
   - **Fix**: Use `git tag -l` instead of `git rev-parse` for reliable tag detection

3. **Changeset in wrong directory** — Changeset file was at root `/.changeset/` instead of `/js/.changeset/`
   - **Fix**: Move changeset to correct location

4. **npm update fails on Node.js 22.22.2** — Known issue ([actions/runner-images#13883](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13883)) causes `npm install -g npm@11` to fail, leaving npm 10.x which doesn't support OIDC
   - **Fix**: Improved error reporting and fallback chain in `setup-npm.mjs`

5. **Rust GitHub release created regardless of publish result** — Could create a release even when `cargo publish` failed
   - **Fix**: Condition `Create GitHub Release` step on `steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'`

### Changes

- `scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` — Replace `changeset publish` with `npm publish --provenance --access public`, add post-publish verification
- `scripts/rust-version-check.mjs` — Use `git tag -l` instead of `git rev-parse` for tag detection
- `scripts/setup-npm.mjs` — Better error reporting for npm update failures with version check fallback
- `.github/workflows/rust.yml` — Condition GitHub release on successful crates.io publish
- `.changeset/ → js/.changeset/` — Move changeset to correct directory
- `docs/case-studies/issue-40/` — Full case study with timeline, evidence, and root cause analysis

- [ ] After merge, verify JS release workflow publishes to npm successfully
- [ ] After merge, verify Rust release workflow triggers and publishes to crates.io (requires `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret)

title: Add Google Docs (document to markdown) support
body:
## Summary

Implements Google Docs document capture support, addressing all requirements from issue #36:

- **Google Docs capture module** (`gdocs.js` / `gdocs.rs`): Detects Google Docs URLs, extracts document IDs, and fetches documents via the Google Docs export URL pattern (`/export?format=html|md|txt|pdf|docx|epub|zip`)
- **API token support**: `--apiToken` CLI option and `API_TOKEN` environment variable for private document access. API server supports `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `X-Api-Token` headers
- **`/gdocs` API endpoint**: New endpoint in both Express.js and Axum servers
- **Auto-detection**: CLI automatically detects Google Docs URLs and uses API-based capture
- **Configurable capture**: `--capture` option to choose between `browser` and `api` capture methods
- **Archive mode**: `format=archive` extracts embedded base64 images from Google Docs HTML exports and bundles them with markdown and HTML into a ZIP archive (`article.md`, `article.html`, `images/`)
- **HTML entity decoding**: All HTML and Markdown extraction pipelines decode HTML entities to unicode characters (e.g., `&` → `&`, `—` → `—`) using `html-escape` (Rust) and `he` (JS)
- **Unicode by default**: All export methods request data in UTF-8 and convert to unicode
- **Rust tests reorganized**: All tests moved from inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules in `src/` to separate test files in `tests/` folder for better visibility and organization
- **lino-arguments updated** from `^0.2.1` to `^0.2.5` (latest)
- **JS and Rust in sync**: Both implementations have identical functionality

|------|-------------|
| `js/src/gdocs.js` | Google Docs capture: URL detection, export URL construction, fetch, archive mode, image extraction |
| `rust/src/gdocs.rs` | Rust Google Docs capture module (matching JS) with archive and image extraction |
| `js/src/index.js` | Register `/gdocs` endpoint |
| `rust/src/main.rs` | Add `/gdocs` endpoint with archive/zip format support |

### HTML Entity Decoding

| `js/src/gdocs.js` | Decode HTML entities for text-based export formats |

### Test Reorganization

|------|-------------|
| `rust/tests/*_tests.rs` | 14 test files moved from inline modules (110+ tests total) |
| `js/tests/unit/gdocs.test.js` | 27 unit tests including image extraction tests |

## Test plan

### New Rust modules (9 files, synced with JavaScript)

| Module | Requirement | Description |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| `latex.rs` | R1 | LaTeX formula extraction from Habr, KaTeX, MathJax (using `scraper`) |
| `metadata.rs` | R1 | Article metadata extraction (Habr selectors, LD+JSON with `serde_json`) |
| `postprocess.rs` | R1 | Markdown post-processing: unicode normalization, LaTeX spacing, bold fixes |

| `verify.rs` | R6 | Content verification with fuzzy matching and multiple content checks |

**JavaScript:**
- **`lib.js`**: Added `convertHtmlToMarkdownEnhanced()` with configurable LaTeX extraction, metadata extraction, code language detection, and post-processing pipeline

## Summary

Upgrades `browser-commander` from v0.4.0 to v0.8.0 and migrates all `rawPage` workarounds to browser-commander's new first-class APIs.

**What was the problem:**

In v0.4.0, browser-commander only provided `launchBrowser()` returning raw `{ browser, page }`. All advanced features (PDF, color scheme, keyboard, dialogs, evaluate) required bypassing the library with `rawPage.*` hacks.

**What changed between v0.4.0 and v0.8.0:**

| Version | New APIs |
|---|---|
| v0.6.0 | `commander.page` escape hatch officially documented |
| v0.7.0 | `emulateMedia()`, `keyboard.press/type/down/up`, `onDialog/offDialog/clearDialogHandlers` |
| v0.8.0 | `commander.pdf({ pdfOptions })` |

title: feat: add CLI support for local command and server mode
body:
## Summary

This PR implements CLI support for web-capture, allowing it to work both as a local command for AI agents and as an HTTP API server. The implementation uses the [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) pattern for unified configuration management.

### Key Features

- **Server Mode**: `web-capture --serve` starts the HTTP API server
- **Capture Mode**: `web-capture <url>` captures a URL to file or stdout
- **Multiple Formats**: Support for HTML, Markdown, and PNG screenshot output
- **Browser Engine Selection**: Choose between Puppeteer and Playwright engines
- **Unified Configuration**: Uses lino-arguments for CLI args, env vars, and .lenv files
- **Comprehensive CLI Options**: `--format`, `--output`, `--engine`, `--port`, `--configuration`

## Implementation Details

### New Files
- `bin/web-capture.js` - CLI entry point using lino-arguments pattern
- `.lenv` - Default configuration file with PORT and BROWSER_ENGINE settings
- `tests/unit/cli.test.js` - Unit tests for CLI functionality

### Modified Files
- `package.json` - Added `bin` field for CLI, added lino-arguments dependency, bumped version to 1.1.0
- `README.md` - Added CLI usage documentation, configuration section, and examples

## Configuration System

Uses [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) with the following priority chain (highest to lowest):

1. **CLI arguments**: `--port 8080`
2. **Environment variables**: `PORT=8080`
3. **Custom .lenv file**: `--configuration path/to/custom.lenv`
4. **Default .lenv file**: `.lenv` in project root
5. **Built-in defaults**

### .lenv File Format

```lenv
# Server configuration
PORT: 3000

# Browser engine (puppeteer or playwright)
BROWSER_ENGINE: puppeteer
```

## CLI Usage

### Server Mode
```bash
# Start API server on default port 3000
web-capture --serve

# Start on custom port
web-capture --serve --port 8080

# Use custom configuration file
web-capture --serve --configuration /path/to/custom.lenv
```

### Capture Mode
```bash
# Capture URL as HTML to stdout
web-capture https://example.com

# Capture as Markdown to file
web-capture https://example.com --format markdown --output page.md

# Take screenshot using Playwright engine
web-capture https://example.com --format png --engine playwright -o screenshot.png

# Use environment variable for configuration
PORT=8080 web-capture --serve
```

### All Options
```
-c, --configuration  Path to .lenv configuration file
-s, --serve          Start as HTTP API server
-p, --port           Port for server mode (default: 3000)
-f, --format         Output format: html, markdown/md, image/png
-o, --output         Output file path
-e, --engine         Browser engine: puppeteer, playwright
-h, --help           Show help
-v, --version        Show version
```

## Testing

All CLI tests pass (15 tests):
- Help message display with `--help` and `-h` flags
- Version display with `--version` and `-v` flags
- URL validation and error handling
- Format, engine, and output option documentation
- Server mode option documentation
- Configuration system integration

Unit tests verify the CLI argument parsing and help output work correctly with the lino-arguments/yargs integration.

## Fixes

Fixes #19

# Rust
